prettier/prettier (prettier) ### [`v3.4.2`](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#342) [Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.4.1...3.4.2) [diff](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.4.1...3.4.2) ##### Treat U+30A0 & U+30FB in Katakana Block as CJK ([#​16796](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/16796) by [@​tats-u](https://redirect.github.com/tats-u)) Prettier doesn't treat U+30A0 & U+30FB as Japanese. U+30FB is commonly used in Japanese to represent the delimitation of first and last names of non-Japanese people or “and”. The following “C言語・C++・Go・Rust” means “C language & C++ & Go & Rust” in Japanese. ```md C言 語 ・ C++ ・ Go ・ Rust C言語・ C++ ・ Go ・ Rust C言語・C++・Go・Rust ``` U+30A0 can be used as the replacement of the `-` in non-Japanese names (e.g. “Saint-Saëns” (Charles Camille Saint-Saëns) can be represented as “サン゠サーンス” in Japanese), but substituted by ASCII hyphen (U+002D) or U+FF1D (full width hyphen) in many cases (e.g. “サン=サーンス” or “サン＝サーンス”). ##### Fix comments print on class methods with decorators ([#​16891](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/16891) by [@​fisker](https://redirect.github.com/fisker)) ```jsx // Input class A { @​decorator /** * The method description * */ async method(foo: Foo, bar: Bar) { console.log(foo); } } // Prettier 3.4.1 class A { @​decorator async /** * The method description * */ method(foo: Foo, bar: Bar) { console.log(foo); } } // Prettier 3.4.2 class A { @​decorator /** * The method description * */ async method(foo: Foo, bar: Bar) { console.log(foo); } } ``` ##### Fix non-idempotent formatting ([#​16899](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/16899) by [@​seiyab](https://redirect.github.com/seiyab)) This bug fix is not language-specific. You may see similar change in any languages. This fixes regression in 3.4.0 so change caused by it should yield same formatting as 3.3.3. ```jsx // Input
foo longlonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglongl foo , abc
; // Prettier 3.4.1 (first)
foo longlonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglongl foo , abc
; // Prettier 3.4.1 (second)
foo longlonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglongl foo , abc
; // Prettier 3.4.2
foo longlonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglonglongl foo , abc
; ```

title: path parameters are always strings
body:
Fixes #1116 

Counterfact looks at OpenAPI spec to determine the types of parameters in the query, path, or headers and make sure they are parsed to the correct type at runtime (string, number, or boolean -- we don't support arrays yet). 

When using OpenAPI / Swagger v2, the types of parameters are in the `type` property rather than `schema.type`. Counterfact wasn't looking for the `type` property so everything was being left as strings. 

Also, it didn't make a distinction between `number` and `integer`, casting all numbers to integers. With this change integers are parsed with `parseInt()` and numbers are parsed with `parseFloat()`. 

Also booleans were not parsed. Now the string "true" is parsed as `true`; any other string is `false`.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>tj/commander.js (commander)</summary>

### [`v13.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1300-2024-12-30)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/compare/v12.1.0...v13.0.0)

##### Added

-   support multiple calls to `.parse()` with default settings (\[[#​2299](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2299)])
-   add `.saveStateBeforeParse()` and `.restoreStateBeforeParse()` for use by subclasses (\[[#​2299](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2299)])
-   style routines like `styleTitle()` to add color to help using `.configureHelp()` or Help subclass (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])
-   color related support in `.configureOutput()` for `getOutHasColors()`, `getErrHasColors()`, and `stripColor()` (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])
-   Help property for `minWidthToWrap` (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])
-   Help methods for `displayWidth()`, `boxWrap()`, `preformatted()` et al (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])

##### Changed

-   *Breaking*: excess command-arguments cause an error by default, see migration tips (\[[#​2223](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2223)])
-   *Breaking*: throw during Option construction for unsupported option flags, like multiple characters after single `-` (\[[#​2270](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2270)])
-   *Breaking*: throw on multiple calls to `.parse()` if `storeOptionsAsProperties: true` (\[[#​2299](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2299)])
-   TypeScript: include implicit `this` in parameters for action handler callback (\[[#​2197](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2197)])

##### Deleted

-   *Breaking*: `Help.wrap()` refactored into `formatItem()` and `boxWrap()` (\[[#​2251](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2251)])

##### Migration Tips

**Excess command-arguments**

It is now an error for the user to specify more command-arguments than are expected. (`allowExcessArguments` is now false by default.)

Old code:

```js
program.option('-p, --port <number>', 'port number');
program.action((options) => {
  console.log(program.args);
});
```

Now shows an error:

```console
$ node example.js a b c
error: too many arguments. Expected 0 arguments but got 3.
```

You can declare the expected arguments. The help will then be more accurate too. Note that declaring
new arguments will change what is passed to the action handler.

```js
program.option('-p, --port <number>', 'port number');
program.argument('[args...]', 'remote command and arguments'); // expecting zero or more arguments
program.action((args, options) => {
  console.log(args);
});
```

Or you could suppress the error, useful for minimising changes in legacy code.

```js
program.option('-p, --port', 'port number');
program.allowExcessArguments();
program.action((options) => {
  console.log(program.args);
});
```

</details>

  return $.response[400];
};

body: The problem my team is having is that the schemas we're working with don't reliably have response fields correctly marked as `required`, when in fact almost all of the fields are required (i.e. in real-world usage all fields will be present in responses). As a result we're having to hard-code a lot of responses. I see that json-schema-faker has an `alwaysFakeOptionals` option. Would it be possible to have an option in Counterfact to set this option to `true`?

title: feat: Add alwaysFakeOptionals command line option
body:
Here is a first take on adding the --always-fake-optionals command line option. At first I tried to add the negative case where not having this true would mean optionals are undefined, but that's not a valid test since sometimes JSONSchemaFaker provides random optionals and sometimes not (which is the allowed behavior). So I can't test the default behavior, but we should expect that turning them on is always true. Again, my trouble here is, this isn't a deterministic test since sometimes and optional can be faked even without the switch on. So it could have a false positive, but should never be negative.

Lastly, I threw in there the other two options of `fixedProbabilities` and `optionalsProbability` because from reading it seems those should be set for this to fully work. It was unclear to me if setting `alwaysFakeOptionals` already sets both of those others, but after reading various GitHub issues in the JSF repo I just opted to explicitly turn them all on.

### [`v3.5.2`](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#352)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.5.1...3.5.2)

[diff](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/compare/3.5.1...3.5.2)

##### Remove `module-sync` condition ([#​17156](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17156) by [@​fisker](https://redirect.github.com/fisker))

In Prettier 3.5.0, [we added `module-sync` condition to `package.json`](https://prettier.io/blog/2025/02/09/3.5.0#use-esm-entrypoint-for-requireesm-16958-by-tats-u), so that `require("prettier")` can use ESM version, but turns out it doesn't work if CommonJS and ESM plugins both imports builtin plugins. To solve this problem, we decide simply remove the `module-sync` condition, so `require("prettier")` will still use the CommonJS version, we'll revisit until `require(ESM)` feature is more stable.

</details>

title: counterfact does not support $ref with external yaml files
body:
As the title says, counterfact does not seem to support referencing yaml files in the openapi specification. 
Example:

```yaml
paths:
  /metrics:
    get:
      operationId: getMetrics
      tags:
        - Default
      responses:
        '200':
          description: Successful response
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: 'components/metrics.yaml#/components/schemas/MetricsResponse'
              examples:
                default:
                  $ref: 'components/examples.yaml#/examples/MetricsResponseExample'
        '500':
          description: Internal server error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: 'components/errors.yaml#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse'
```

When opening the swagger docs, I see the following error:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01981e94-b8ef-4b84-b68a-7c486b37e918)

Response schema

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d61295e-1a7a-4184-8252-1c138d437c0c)

When using a single openapi spec file, it works as expected

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb292a0e-1b13-4fbb-87c5-11b4660127b4)

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2025-32379](https://redirect.github.com/koajs/koa/security/advisories/GHSA-x2rg-q646-7m2v)

### Summary
In koa < 2.16.1 and < 3.0.0-alpha.5, passing untrusted user input to ctx.redirect() even after sanitizing it, may execute javascript code on the user who use the app.

### Patches
This issue is patched in  2.16.1 and 3.0.0-alpha.5.

### PoC
https://gist.github.com/linhnph05/03d677b183636af206ff781bdd19701a

### Impact
1. Redirect user to another phishing site
2. Make request to another endpoint of the application based on user's cookie
3. Steal user's cookie

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>tj/commander.js (commander)</summary>

### [`v14.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#1400-2025-05-18)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/compare/v13.1.0...v14.0.0)

##### Added

-   support for groups of options and commands in the help using low-level `.helpGroup()` on `Option` and `Command`, and higher-level `.optionsGroup()` and `.commandsGroup()` which can be used in chaining way to specify group title for following options/commands (\[[#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2328)])
-   support for unescaped negative numbers as option-arguments and command-arguments (\[[#​2339](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2339)])
-   TypeScript: add `parseArg` property to `Argument` class (\[[#​2359](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2359)])

##### Fixed

-   remove bogus leading space in help when option has default value but not a description (\[[#​2348](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2348)])
-   `.configureOutput()` now makes copy of settings instead of modifying in-place, fixing side-effects (\[[#​2350](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2350)])

##### Changed

-   *Breaking:* Commander 14 requires Node.js v20 or higher
-   internal refactor of `Help` class adding `.formatItemList()` and `.groupItems()` methods (\[[#​2328](https://redirect.github.com/tj/commander.js/issues/2328)])

title: feat: mock service worker handler ability
body:
Adds two new functions to the app: 

`createMswHandlers`
and 
`handleMswRequest`

These can be used to generate a set of mock service worker handlers that allow MSW to hand off requests to Counterfact. 

Presently this is somewhat narrowly written with Vitest Browser mode in mind where Vitest communicates with Counterfact through the Custom Commands concept where there is a bridge between the browser and node. A future update might allow the Counterfact Dispatcher to run entirely in the browser and eliminate the need for the two stage setup.

title: Add startup option for building the cache
body: The current implementation only transpiles the routes and contexts when you start the server. The transpiler presently only runs in the `start()` function returned by the `counterfact` function and only when the `startServer` option is true. We should have a CLI option to transpile the code to cache without running the server so that test environments can buid the cache as part of the test harness startup. This will be necessary for the new MSW functionality because without it the user has to be sure they have started CF at least once.

title: Add Prune option for clearing out defunct paths and endpoints
body:
Sometimes an OpenApi spec might change path names or endpoint names. In that case, if a consumer tries to run Counterfact again, since it will leave the old paths and routes alone it is possible to end up with multiple wild card routes at the same end path. Example:

Old path:
`/pet/{id}/update/{Name}.ts`
New path:
`/pet/{id}/update/{nickname}.ts`

In this case, the old file will be left in place and the new one created. Then when `module-tree.ts` attempts to resolve the path it will have ambiguity because both wildcards can be a math if they both have the same HTTP verb.

We should offer a `--prune` option that will clean out any paths that aren't represented in the OpenApi spec.

title: Add Warning to Module Tree if Ambiguous Wildcards Detected
body: While it is invalid API spec to have two wildcard paths at the same path defined (see issue #1308) it is possible to end up in a state where you have two such as the referenced issue or from just manually creating a second endpoint. The `module-tree.ts` class has enough logic in place to be aware that more than a single leaf wildcard path has been found for a given path. We should at the least show a console log warning when this is detected to raise awareness to the consumer.

##### TypeScript: Allow const without initializer ([#​17650](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17650), [#​17654](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17654) by [@​fisker](https://redirect.github.com/fisker))

<!-- prettier-ignore -->

```jsx
// Input
export const version: string;

// Prettier 3.6.0 (--parser=babel-ts)
SyntaxError: Unexpected token (1:21)
> 1 | export const version: string;
    |                     ^

// Prettier 3.6.0 (--parser=oxc-ts)
SyntaxError: Missing initializer in const declaration (1:14)
> 1 | export const version: string;
    |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

// Prettier 3.6.1
export const version: string;
```

##### Miscellaneous: Avoid closing files multiple times ([#​17665](https://redirect.github.com/prettier/prettier/pull/17665) by [@​43081j](https://redirect.github.com/43081j))

When reading a file to infer the interpreter from a shebang, we use the
`n-readlines` library to read the first line in order to get the shebang.

This library closes files when it reaches EOF, and we later try close the same
files again. We now close files only if `n-readlines` did not already close
them.

</details>

title: feat: Auto-detect native TypeScript execution support
body:
## Summary

Allows Counterfact to run with no transpilation when the runtime natively supports TypeScript type stripping (e.g. `tsx`, `ts-node`, or Node.js with `--experimental-strip-types`). Rather than requiring a CLI flag, the server probes the runtime at startup and automatically serves routes directly from the `routes/` directory when native TypeScript execution is available, falling back to the existing `.cache`-based transpilation otherwise.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

The goal is to allow running Counterfact with no transpilation at all. In my tests so far you can run this with TSX directly against the `routes` folder, no need for `.cache`.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] When running with `tsx` (e.g. `tsx src/app.ts`) or `node --experimental-strip-types`, the server starts without creating a `.cache` directory and serves routes directly from `routes/`
- [x] When running with standard `node` (no TypeScript support), the server creates and uses a `.cache/` directory for transpiled output, matching prior behavior
- [x] TypeScript route handlers are executed correctly in native TS mode (type annotations do not cause runtime errors)
- [x] Existing routes and behavior are unchanged when running in the default (non-native TS) execution mode
- [x] Switching from a native-TS runtime to a standard Node runtime (or vice versa) does not break the server or leave stale cache artifacts

## Tasks

- Implement `runtimeCanExecuteErasableTs()` in `src/util/runtime-can-execute-erasable-ts.ts` — writes a temporary `.ts` probe file and attempts to `import()` it to detect runtime capability
- Replace the `useTsx` config option with the automatic runtime detection in `app.ts`
- Conditionally skip transpiler startup and `.cache` cleanup when native TS execution is detected
- Treat `.ts` files as ES modules in `src/server/determine-module-kind.ts`
- Add a unit test for `runtimeCanExecuteErasableTs`

title: Counterfact generating invalid types for date-time field
body:
I'm using Counterfact on a schema:

```yaml
FooResponse:
  type: object
  properties:
    settingName:
      type: string
      description: Name of setting
    settingId:
      type: string
      format: uuid
      description: Identifier for disclaimer
    settingValue:
      type: string
      description: Value of the disclaimer
    createdOn:
      type: date-time
    modifiedOn:
      type: date-time
```

When I run Counterfact, the following error appears:

```
SyntaxError: ';' expected. (3:124)
  1 |
  2 |
> 3 | export type FooResponse = {"settingName"?: string,"settingId"?: string,"settingValue"?: string,"createdOn"?: date-time,"modifiedOn"?: date-time};
    |                                                                                                                  ^
    at _4 (file:///Users/JRunning/xxxxxxx/node_modules/counterfact/node_modules/prettier/plugins/typescript.mjs:17:70566)
    at N4 (file:///Users/JRunning/xxxxxxx/node_modules/counterfact/node_modules/prettier/plugins/typescript.mjs:20:955)
    at Object.M4 [as parse] (file:///Users/JRunning/xxxxxxx/node_modules/counterfact/node_modules/prettier/plugins/typescript.mjs:20:1477)
    ...
```

I think Counterfact should be generating a `string` type there instead of using `date-time` verbatim.

title: MaybeShortcut for content type is too strict
body:
Openapi library, which I am using, uses `application/json; charset=utf-8` for json responses as content type. Current `MaybeShortcut` implementation expects exact match of content type which make json field not available. My suggestion is to use contains instead of exact content match. Like so:
```ts
type IfHasKey<
  SomeObject,
  Keys extends readonly string[],
  Yes,
  No,
> = Keys extends [infer FirstKey, ...infer RestKeys]
  ? Extract<
      keyof SomeObject,
      `${string}${FirstKey & string}${string}`
    > extends never
    ? IfHasKey<SomeObject, RestKeys & readonly string[], Yes, No>
    : Yes
  : No;
```

title: Colon in filenames not supported in Windows
body:
Hi,
I have a "weird" OpenAPI spec where they use colons in their paths to distinguish different endpoints, much like Wikipedia does (e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk:Main_Page). This is perfectly valid for URLs.

The issue with counterfact is that these paths cause the route file names to have the colons in them, which is perfectly fine on macOS/Linux, but not at all supported on Windows/NTFS. Git on macOS even warns me about that before commiting.

So I think this needs to be changed somehow, since there is no easy workaround I could think of apart from editing that OpenAPI spec file, which is not something I should be forced to do.

title: fix(deps): update dependency koa to v3.0.3 [security]
body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | Age | Confidence | |---|---|---|---| | [koa](https://koajs.com) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/koajs/koa)) | [`3.0.1` -> `3.0.3`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/koa/3.0.1/3.0.3) | [![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/koa/3.0.3?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/koa/3.0.1/3.0.3?slim=true)](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | ### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts #### [CVE-2025-62595](https://redirect.github.com/koajs/koa/security/advisories/GHSA-g8mr-fgfg-5qpc) ### Summary: A bypass was discovered in the `Koa.js` framework affecting its back redirect functionality. In certain circumstances, an attacker can manipulate the Referer header to force a user’s browser to navigate to an external, potentially malicious website. This occurs because the implementation incorrectly treats some specially crafted URLs as safe relative paths. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow attackers to perform phishing, social engineering, or other redirect-based attacks on users of affected applications. This vulnerability affects the code referenced in GitHub Advisory GHSA-jgmv-j7ww-jx2x (which is tracked as CVE‑2025‑54420). ### Details: The patched code attempts to treat values that `startWith('/')` as safe relative paths and only perform origin checks for absolute URLs. However, protocol‑relative URLs (those beginning with //host) also start with '/' and therefore match the startsWith('/') branch. A protocol‑relative referrer such as `//evil.com` with trailing double-slash is treated by the implementation as a safe relative path, but browsers interpret Location: //evil.com as a redirect to https://evil.com (or http:// based on context). This discrepancy allows an attacker to supply Referer: //evil.com and trigger an external redirect - bypassing the intended same‑origin protection. ### Proof of concept (PoC): Affected line of code: https://github.com/koajs/koa/blob/master/lib/response.js#L326 The problematic logic looks like: Request with a protocol‑relative Referer: curl -i -H "Referer: //haymiz.dev" http://127.0.0.1:3000/test Vulnerable response will contain: HTTP/1.1 302 Found Location: //haymiz.dev A browser receiving that Location header navigates to https://haymiz.dev (or http:// depending on context), resulting in an open redirect to an attacker‑controlled host: ### Recommendation / Patch: * Do not treat //host as a safe relative path. Explicitly exclude protocol‑relative values from any relative‑path branch. * Normalize the Referer by resolving it with a base (e.g., new URL(rawRef, ctx.href)), then compare resolved.origin (scheme+host+port) to ctx.origin (or ctx.host plus scheme/port) before allowing the redirect. ### Impact: An attacker who can cause a victim to visit a specially crafted link (or inject a request with a controlled Referer) can cause the victim to be redirected to an attacker‑controlled domain. This can be used for phishing, social engineering, or to bypass some protection rules that rely on same‑origin navigation. --- ### Release Notes

title: Raise error for schema name conflict
body:
In our use case we're merging multiple YAML files before using Counterfact to generate types from them. Occasionally two different files will have two schema with the same name, in which case Counterfact silently generates only one `.ts` file, presumably corresponding to whichever schema it processed second (i.e. the second overwrites the first).

This failure mode can be tricky to detect manually, as often the two schema are similar enough in shape that it doesn't immediately cause TS errors. It would be nice if Counterfact would warn us by raising an error (detectable in CI) when it encounters multiple schema with the same name.

title: Optional parameters are marked as required when they reference a schema with a required property containing list of sub properties
body:
Reference

For a OpenAPI spec like:

```yaml
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Minimal Reproduction
  version: 1.0.0
paths: {}
components:
  schemas:
    Example:
      type: object
      properties:
        requiredField:
          type: string
        optionalObjectWithRequiredSubField:
          type: object
          properties:
            subField:
              type: string
          required:
            - subField   # <-- this nested required array causes counterfact to
                         #     incorrectly mark optionalObjectWithRequiredSubField
                         #     as required at the parent level
      required:
        - requiredField  # optionalObjectWithRequiredSubField is intentionally absent
```

The expected generated TypeScript type would be:

```typescript
type Example = {
  requiredField: string;
  optionalObjectWithRequiredSubField?: { subField: string };  // should be optional
};
```

but the actual result is incorrect like so:

```typescript
type Example = {
  requiredField: string;
  optionalObjectWithRequiredSubField: { subField: string };  // incorrectly required
};
```

title: Midleware matching all routes is not executed
fix(operation-type-coder): sanitize operation ID before generating type
body:
Attempts to fix an issue in `operation-type-coder` when using an OpenAPI `operationId` value as a TypeScript parameter name. Previously we used the `operationId` value verbatim which leads to TypeScript syntax errors when invalid TypeScript identifier characters were present. 

This fix sanitizes the `operationId` value removing invalid special characters and camelCasing the output. If an `operationId` starts with a digit it is prefixed with a `_`.

If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## counterfact@2.0.1

### Patch Changes

-   3a7046b: Sanitize `operationId` values before using them as TypeScript identifiers in generated code.

    Previously, any `operationId` from an OpenAPI spec was used verbatim, which could produce invalid TypeScript when the value contained hyphens, dots, spaces, or other characters not permitted in identifiers. The value is now converted to camelCase (e.g. `get-user-profile` → `getUserProfile`) and any remaining invalid characters are stripped.

title: Fix root middleware not executed for any routes
body:
Root-level `_.middleware.ts` (placed in the `routes/` folder) was silently skipped — it never ran for any route.

The `recurse()` function in `registry.ts` walked path segments from deepest to root by stripping trailing segments, but bottomed out at `""` instead of `"/"`. Since the module-loader registers root middleware under key `"/"`, it was never matched.

**Changes:**
- **`src/server/registry.ts`**: Fix `nextPath` calculation so traversal ends at `"/"` rather than `""`, before terminating at `null`:
  ```ts
  // Before: /devices → "" → null  (never checks "/")
  // After:  /devices → "/" → null  (root middleware matched)
  const nextPath =
    path === "/" || path === ""
      ? null
      : path.slice(0, path.lastIndexOf("/")) || "/";
  ```
- **`test/server/registry.test.ts`**: Update existing middleware tests to register root middleware under `"/"` (consistent with module-loader), and add a focused regression test for the root middleware case.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Midleware matching all routes is not executed</issue_title>
> <issue_description>Hey,
> 
> I am using counterfact@1.5.0.
> 
> 
> Assume the following definition of a middleware
> ```typescript
> //_.middleware.ts
> export async function middleware($: any, respondTo: any) {
>   const response = await respondTo($);
>   console.log(`received request to ${$.matchedPath} -> ${response.status}`);
>   return response;
> }
> ```
> 
> If I place the file in the subfolder of any route, the middleware is executed for all (sub-)routes in that folder.
> If the middleware is defined in the root-folder (`routes`), it is not executed at all.
> 
> As described in https://github.com/pmcelhaney/counterfact/issues/1170, the middleware should actually be ececuted for any path.
> 
> IMHO the problem liys in the definition of the `recurse`-function in `registry.ts`: When the last path segment (e.g. "/devices") is handled, the leading "/" is omitted, so a root-middleware (which is inserted with the URL "/") is never called.

title: Add JSON prettification middleware for HTTP responses
body:
JSON responses from the server were returned as compact, unformatted strings, making them difficult to read directly.

## Changes

- **`src/server/create-koa-app.ts`**: Adds a middleware (placed before `koaMiddleware`) that post-processes responses using Koa's onion model — calls `await next()` to let downstream middleware set `ctx.body`, then prettifies plain object bodies with 2-space indentation and sets `Content-Type: application/json`. title: fix: pass CI automatically on docs-only PRs
body:
The CI workflow's `paths-ignore: "**/*.md"` rule caused it to skip entirely on docs-only PRs. When a workflow never runs, GitHub leaves required status checks in "Pending" — permanently blocking the PR from merging.

## Change

- Removed `paths-ignore` from `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` so the workflow always triggers on PRs targeting `main`
- Added a lightweight `filter` job that detects whether any non-`.md` files changed
- The `ci-checks` job now runs only when `filter` reports non-docs changes (`if: needs.filter.outputs.non-docs == 'true'`)

When a PR touches only `.md` files, `ci-checks` is skipped. GitHub reports skipped jobs (via `if:` conditions) as **"Success"**, satisfying the required status check without running the full suite. Code-changing PRs run CI as normal.

title: Add comprehensive type tests for counterfact-types and wire into CI
body:
`counterfact-types` had only minimal type tests covering `OmitAll` and `IfHasKey`, with the `test:tsd` script not running in CI at all.

## Changes

- **`test/server/types.test-d.ts`** — Added `tsd`-based type tests for all major exported types:
  - `MaybePromise<T>` — accepts `T` and `Promise<T>`, rejects unrelated types
  - `OmitValueWhenNever` — removes `never`-valued keys, preserves others
  - `HttpStatusCode` — accepts valid codes (200, 404, 500), rejects non-standard (0, 999)
  - `MediaType` — accepts `"a/b"` patterns, rejects strings without a slash
  - `GenericResponseBuilderInner` — verifies shortcut methods (`json`, `html`, `text`) are present only when the matching content type is in the response, and `header` is present only when response headers exist
  - `ResponseBuilderFactory` — verifies status codes map to appropriate builder shapes
  - `OpenApiResponse` — verifies the interface is satisfied by a well-formed response

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`** — Added a **Type Tests** step that builds and runs `yarn test:tsd`:
  ```yaml
  - name: Type Tests
    timeout-minutes: 2
    run: yarn build && yarn test:tsd
  ```

The `tsd` command requires the compiled output (`dist/`), so the build step is included inline.

title: Return HTTP 405 when path exists but method is not registered
body:
Previously, any unmatched request returned 404 regardless of whether the URL path existed — making it impossible to distinguish "path not found" from "method not allowed".

## Changes

- **`src/server/dispatcher.ts`**: Added an early-return 405 check in `request()` — if the path is registered but the requested method has no handler, returns 405 with an `Allow` header listing the valid methods; 404 is still returned when the path itself is not found.
- **`src/server/registry.ts`**: Added `ALL_HTTP_METHODS` constant, `pathExistsWithAnyMethod(url, excludeMethod)`, and `allowedMethods(url)` as public methods used by the dispatcher.
- **`test/server/dispatcher.test.ts`**: Added 405 tests for exact paths and wildcard paths.
- **`.changeset/return-405-for-unregistered-methods.md`**: Added a changeset file (type `patch`) to document the change for release management.

## Example

```ts
registry.add("/hello", { GET() { return { body: "hi", status: 200 }; } });

// Before: POST /hello → 404
// After:  POST /hello → 405, Allow: GET
```

title: feat: automatically create changesets for Renovate PRs
body:
Renovate dependency update PRs were not generating changesets, so they were excluded from release notes.

Adds `.github/workflows/renovate-changesets.yaml` that triggers on `pull_request_target` for `renovate[bot]` PRs and automatically commits a `patch` changeset to the PR branch.

## Key behaviors

- **Idempotent**: skips if `.changeset/` already contains a file, no `package.json` changed, or branch doesn't start with `renovate/`
- **Diff-based message**: parses `package.json` diff lines to produce per-dependency entries (e.g. `` Updated dependency `typescript` to `5.4.0`. ``); falls back to PR title if parsing yields nothing
- **Safe checkout**: guards against fork PRs with `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository` — prevents untrusted code execution in a privileged `pull_request_target` context
- **Non-destructive commit**: adds a new commit rather than amending Renovate's commit, avoiding force-push conflicts

## Example generated changeset

```md
---
'counterfact': patch
---

Updated dependency `typescript` to `5.4.0`.
Updated dependency `@types/node` to `20.11.0`.
```

When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## counterfact@2.2.1

### Patch Changes

-   304cbfe: Add `example(name)` method to response builder for selecting named OpenAPI examples

    Developers can now select a specific named example from the OpenAPI specification using the strongly-typed `example()` method on a response builder:

    ```ts
    return $.response[200].example("namedExample1");
    ```

    The method is fully type-safe: TypeScript will autocomplete the example names defined in the OpenAPI document and report a type error if an unknown name is used.

    Example names are collected from the `examples` field of each media type in the response content (OpenAPI 3.x). The method can be chained with other response builder methods:

    ```ts
    return $.response[200]
      .example("namedExample1")
      .header("some-header", "some-value");
    ```

title: Add --prune option to remove defunct route files when OpenAPI spec changes
body:
When an OpenAPI spec renames a path parameter (e.g., `{Name}` → `{nickname}`), both the old and new route files coexist, creating wildcard ambiguity in `ModuleTree` resolution. The `--prune` flag removes route files that no longer exist in the spec before generating new ones.

## Changes

- **`src/typescript-generator/prune.js`** — New `pruneRoutes(destination, openApiPaths)` function: walks `routes/`, deletes `.ts` files with no matching spec path, removes empty directories post-prune. `_.context.ts` files are always preserved.
- **`src/typescript-generator/generate.js`** — Calls `pruneRoutes()` when `generateOptions.prune && generateOptions.routes`, before writing new files.
- **`src/server/config.ts`** — Adds optional `prune?: boolean` to the `generate` config shape.
- **`src/typescript-generator/code-generator.ts`** — Updates constructor/field types to accept `prune?`.
- **`bin/counterfact.js`** — Adds `--prune` CLI flag wired into `config.generate.prune`.
- **`test/typescript-generator/prune.test.js`** — 7 tests covering file deletion, context file preservation, empty-dir cleanup, root path (`/` → `index.ts`), no-op when all files match, and missing `routes/` directory.
- **`.changeset/add-prune-option.md`** — Changeset entry documenting this as a minor release.

## Example

```sh
# After renaming {Name} to {nickname} in the spec:
npx counterfact openapi.yaml ./out --generate --prune
# Deletes routes/pet/{id}/update/{Name}.ts before generating routes/pet/{id}/update/{nickname}.ts
```

> <issue_description>Sometimes an OpenApi spec might change path names or endpoint names. In that case, if a consumer tries to run Counterfact again, since it will leave the old paths and routes alone it is possible to end up with multiple wild card routes at the same end path. Example:
> 
> Old path:
> `/pet/{id}/update/{Name}.ts`
> New path:
> `/pet/{id}/update/{nickname}.ts`

> In this case, the old file will be left in place and the new one created. Then when `module-tree.ts` attempts to resolve the path it will have ambiguity because both wildcards can be a math if they both have the same HTTP verb.

title: Support for external YAML files
body:
Fixes Swagger UI resolver errors that occurred when an OpenAPI spec referenced schemas in external YAML files via `$ref` (e.g., `components/metrics.yaml#/components/schemas/MetricsResponse`). The `/counterfact/openapi` middleware now uses `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser`'s `bundle()` to inline all external references into a single self-contained spec before serving it, so Swagger UI can resolve schemas without fetching sibling files.

## Changes Made

- **`src/server/openapi-middleware.ts`**: Uses `bundle()` to dereference external `$ref` targets and serve a fully self-contained OpenAPI document.
- **`test/server/openapi-middleware.test.ts`**: Added unit tests verifying that external `$ref`s are fully inlined (no external file references remain in the bundled output). Fixed import extension from `.ts` to `.js` to match the Jest ESM convention.
- **`package.json`**: Pinned `@types/node` to `17.0.45` so its major version matches the minimum supported Node version in `engines`.
- **`renovate.json`**: Configured Renovate to not automatically update `@types/node` (its major version should match the `engines` field in `package.json`).
- **`yarn.lock`**: Regenerated after merging `main` to resolve conflicts and include the pinned `@types/node@17.0.45`.

## Manual Acceptance Criteria

- [x] retest the original issue (seems like it was working before his change)
- [x] follow the steps below and make sure that Swagger is working now

1. Create a main OpenAPI spec file (e.g., `openapi.yaml`) that references external YAML files via `$ref`:

   ```yaml
   openapi: "3.0.0"
   info:
     title: Test API
     version: "1.0.0"
   paths:
     /metrics:
       get:
         operationId: getMetrics
         responses:
           '200':
             description: Successful response
             content:
               application/json:
                 schema:
                   $ref: 'components/schemas.yaml#/components/schemas/MetricsResponse'
   ```

2. Create the referenced external file at `components/schemas.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   components:
     schemas:
       MetricsResponse:
         type: object
         properties:
           data:
             type: array
             items:
               type: string
   ```

3. Start counterfact pointing at the main spec:

   ```bash
   npx counterfact@latest openapi.yaml api
   ```

4. Open the Swagger UI at `http://localhost:3100/_counterfact/`.

5. **Expected:** The `/metrics` endpoint shows the `MetricsResponse` schema fully expanded with no resolver errors.

6. **Before this fix:** Swagger UI showed resolver errors (`Could not resolve reference: undefined undefined`) and the schema field displayed the raw `$ref` string instead of the resolved schema.

title: Add API Testing GUI with Postman-like interface
body:
Implements a browser-based API testing interface at `/counterfact/test-api` that's tightly integrated with Counterfact's unique features: per-endpoint proxy toggling, context state management, and direct links to route handler code.

## Implementation

**New Vue.js 3 UI** (`src/client/api-tester.html.hbs`)
- Route browser sidebar with method badges
- Request builder: method/URL/headers/body with tabbed interface
- Response viewer: status, headers, body with JSON formatting
- Per-endpoint proxy toggle using existing admin API (`/_counterfact/api/config/proxy`)
- Context editor for stateful mock manipulation (`/_counterfact/api/contexts`)
- VSCode deep links to route handler source files

**Server integration**
- Added `/counterfact/test-api` route in `create-koa-app.ts`
- Registered `json` Handlebars helper in `page-middleware.ts` for data serialization
- Updated dashboard to include "API Tester" navigation button

## Example Usage

After starting Counterfact, navigate to `http://localhost:3100/counterfact/test-api`:

1. Select a route from the sidebar (e.g., `GET /hello/{name}`)
2. Toggle proxy on/off to switch between mock and real backend
3. Edit request headers/body in tabs
4. View context state and modify it to affect subsequent requests
5. Click "Edit in VSCode" to jump directly to the route handler code

Unlike generic API testers, this UI exposes Counterfact's stateful mocking and hybrid proxy capabilities directly in the testing workflow.

title: Convert black-box tests from Jest/Node to Python
body:
Migrates Counterfact's black-box integration tests from Jest/Node to Python/pytest to better validate the CLI/server behavior as an external process.

## Changes Made

- **`test-black-box/openapi.yaml`** - Dedicated OpenAPI spec for the black-box test suite with three routes (`/ping`, `/items`, `/path/with:colon`), each with exactly one response example so generated handlers return deterministic, assertable values
- **`test-black-box/conftest.py`** - Session-scoped pytest fixture that starts Counterfact as a subprocess in an isolated OS temp directory using `test-black-box/openapi.yaml`; writes server stdout/stderr to a log file (avoiding Windows pipe-buffer deadlocks); `wait_for_server()` catches all `RequestException` subtypes and requires an HTTP 200 before returning; cleans up with `shutil.rmtree()` after all tests
- **`test-black-box/test_counterfact.py`** - 7 test cases written in idiomatic Python; all `requests.get()` calls use a 10-second timeout; response content is asserted exactly (`response.text == "pong"`, `response.json() == ["apple", "banana", "cherry"]`, etc.); includes a test for the `--spec` CLI flag that runs counterfact in generate-only mode and verifies route files are created
- **`test-black-box/requirements.txt`** - Python dependencies (`pytest>=7.0`, `requests>=2.28`)
- **`bin/counterfact.js`** - Added `--spec <string>` option as an alternative to the positional `[openapi.yaml]` argument
- **`test/black-box.test.js`** - Removed (replaced by Python tests)
- **`test/__snapshots__/black-box.test.js.snap`** - Removed (orphaned snapshot)
- **`package.json`** - `test:black-box` script runs `python3 -m pytest test-black-box/ -v` after building
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`** - Added Python setup and pip install steps; increased Black Box Tests timeout to 5 minutes
- **`.github/copilot-instructions.md`** - Updated repo structure, tech stack, and testing conventions
- **`.gitignore`** - Added Python cache patterns

## Testing

- ✅ All 7 Python black-box tests pass
- ✅ ESLint passes (warnings only, pre-existing)

title: readJson()
Add `readJson()` utility to context constructors
body:
Context files had no ergonomic way to load JSON fixtures — users were forced to use `require()` directly, a leaky abstraction from the CJS hot-reload layer.

## Changes

- **`src/server/module-loader.ts`**: Passes a `readJson` function alongside `loadContext` when constructing `Context` instances. Paths are resolved relative to the `_.context.ts` file's directory. Throws descriptive errors on missing files or invalid JSON.
- **`test/server/module-loader.test.ts`**: Tests basic JSON loading and cross-directory path resolution via `../`.
- **`docs/usage.md`**: Documents the new `readJson` parameter with a typed TypeScript example.

## Usage

```ts
// routes/_.context.ts
export class Context {
  private readonly readJson: (path: string) => Promise<unknown>;

  constructor({ readJson }: { readJson: (path: string) => Promise<unknown> }) {
    this.readJson = readJson;
  }

  async getSeeds() {
    return this.readJson("../mocks/seeds.json"); // relative to this file
  }
}
```

title: Add binary data support in mock responses
body:
## Summary

Adds first-class binary response support to Counterfact's mock response pipeline, aligning handler ergonomics and generated types with OpenAPI's binary response conventions (OAS3 `type: string, format: binary`, OAS2 `type: file`).

Route handlers can now return binary data directly via a new `.binary()` method, accepting either a `Uint8Array` or a base64-encoded string (decoded automatically). All binary type references use `Uint8Array | string` throughout the public API to avoid requiring `@types/node` in consumer projects.

A bug was also fixed where passing a plain `Uint8Array` to `.binary()` caused Koa to JSON-serialize it (e.g. `{"0":1,"1":2,"2":3}`) instead of sending raw binary bytes. The fix ensures `Uint8Array` inputs are always converted to a Node.js `Buffer` before being stored, since Koa only recognizes `Buffer` as binary data.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

Per the OpenApi spec binary responses are allowed:

https://swagger.io/docs/specification/describing-responses/

v3 says to use `"type": "string"` but with `"format": "binary"`.
v2 says to use just `"type": "file"`

Not sure how best to have an endpoint load and respond with binary data but perhaps if a mock had base64 data in a string the endpoint could then decode it before returning the response.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] A route handler returning `$.response[200].binary(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3]))` causes the server to respond with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` and the exact bytes `[1, 2, 3]` (not JSON `{"0":1,"1":2,"2":3}`)
- [x] A route handler returning `$.response[200].binary("SGVsbG8gV29ybGQ=")` (base64) causes the server to respond with the decoded bytes (`Hello World`) and `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`
- [x] After hot-reloading a route file that adds a `.binary()` call, the running server immediately serves the binary response without restart
- [x] An OpenAPI spec with `type: string, format: binary` generates a route handler typed as `Uint8Array | string` (not `Buffer | string`) for the response body
- [x] Existing non-binary routes (`GET /ping`, `GET /items`) behave unchanged after this update

## Tasks

- **`response-builder.ts`** — New `binary(body: Uint8Array | string)` method. Always converts the input to a `Buffer` before storing: base64 strings via `Buffer.from(body, "base64")`, and `Uint8Array` values (including plain ones that are not already a `Buffer`) via `Buffer.from(body)`. This ensures Koa sends the body as binary rather than JSON-serializing it. Stores result as `application/octet-stream`.
- **`registry.ts`** — `CounterfactResponseObject.body` widened from `string` to `Uint8Array | string`.
- **`dispatcher.ts`** — Type cast in `normalizeResponse` updated to pass `Uint8Array` bodies through.
- **`koa-middleware.ts`** — Explicitly sets `ctx.type` from `response.contentType`, ensuring the correct `Content-Type` header is sent (benefits all response types).
- **`schema-type-coder.js`** — Emits `Uint8Array | string` for `{ type: "string", format: "binary" }` (v3) and `{ type: "file" }` (v2) schemas, avoiding a dependency on Node.js `Buffer` typings in generated code.
- **`counterfact-types/index.ts`** — Added `binary` to `ResponseBuilder`, `WideResponseBuilder`, and `GenericResponseBuilderInner` using `Uint8Array | string` for broad TypeScript compatibility without requiring `@types/node`.
- **`test/server/response-builder.test.ts`** — Added test verifying that a plain `Uint8Array` passed to `binary()` is stored as a `Buffer` (not a raw `Uint8Array`), covering the bug fix.
- **`test/server/types.test-d.ts`** — Added `tsd` type tests verifying `binary` is exposed for `application/octet-stream` responses and absent for other content types.
- **`test/server/koa-middleware.test.ts`** — Added test verifying `ctx.type` is correctly set to `application/octet-stream` for binary responses.
- **`test/typescript-generator/schema-type-coder.test.js`** — Updated tests to expect `Uint8Array | string` instead of `Buffer | string`.
- **`test-black-box/openapi.yaml`** — Added `/binary-file` endpoint with OAS3 `type: string, format: binary` response for black-box testing.
- **`test-black-box/test_counterfact.py`** — Added `test_binary_response` black-box test: overwrites the generated handler with one that calls `.binary()` with a base64 payload, polls for hot-reload, then verifies `application/octet-stream` content-type and correct decoded binary body.
- **`.changeset/binary-data-responses.md`** — Changeset documenting the new binary data support feature.

title: Break REPL out of `counterfact()` and expose as public API
Fix IfHasKey to use substring matching for content type keys
body:
`MaybeShortcut` (and thus shortcuts like `.json()`) was unavailable when an OpenAPI spec used content types like `application/json; charset=utf-8` because `IfHasKey` required an exact key match.

## Changes

- **`src/counterfact-types/index.ts`** — Changed `IfHasKey` from exact matching (`keyof SomeObject extends FirstKey`) to substring/contains matching (`Extract<keyof SomeObject, \`${string}${FirstKey}${string}\`> extends never`), consistent with how `OmitAll` already works.
- **`test/server/types.test-d.ts`** — Added a type test asserting `IfHasKey` returns `true` when the object has `application/json; charset=utf-8` as a key and the search term is `application/json`.

```ts
// Before: this would resolve to `never` — no `.json()` shortcut available
type R = {
  content: { "application/json; charset=utf-8": { schema: string } };
  headers: {};
  requiredHeaders: never;
};

// After: IfHasKey correctly matches the key, exposing `.json()`
declare const builder: GenericResponseBuilderInner<R>;
builder.json("hello"); // ✅ now works
```

Current `MaybeShortcut` implementation expects exact match of content type which make json field not available. My suggestion is to use contains instead of exact content match. Like so:

title: Add apiKey support (header, query, cookie) to generated operation types and $.auth
body:
Counterfact ignores the OpenAPI `securitySchemes` object when generating types. This PR adds support for `apiKey` security schemes across all three in-locations (`header`, `query`, `cookie`), both in generated types and at runtime.

### Changes

- **`OperationTypeCoder.writeCode()`** — refactored into a shared `mergeApiKeyFields()` helper that merges apiKey scheme names into the corresponding parameter type (`headers`, `query`, or `cookie`) for all three placements
- **`OperationTypeCoder.authType()`** — generates apiKey field names as required `string` properties on `$.auth`, merged alongside basic-auth fields (`username`/`password`) via `&` intersection when both are present
- **Deduplication** — skips adding an API key field if the operation already explicitly declares a parameter with the same name (the parameter definition wins)
- **Cookie type** — added `cookie` as a new field in the generated `$` argument, exported as `_Cookie` type alongside the existing `_Query`, `_Path`, and `_Headers` types
- **`WideOperationArgument`** — added `cookie: { [key: string]: string }` and `auth: { [key: string]: string | undefined }` so route handlers compile correctly
- **Runtime cookie support** — `koa-middleware.ts` now parses the `Cookie` request header and passes the result to `dispatcher.ts`, which forwards it to route handlers as `$.cookie`
- **Runtime `$.auth` population** — `dispatcher.ts` exposes two new private methods: `extractApiKeyFromRequest()` and `buildAuth()`. The latter merges basic-auth credentials with each `apiKey` scheme's value extracted from the appropriate location (`header`, `query`, or `cookie`), passing the combined result to route handlers as `$.auth`

### Example

Given a spec with:
```yaml
components:
  securitySchemes:
    api_key:
      type: apiKey
      name: api_key
      in: header   # or "query" or "cookie"
```

Operations generate exported types for each location:
```typescript
// in: header
export type getPet_Headers = { "api_key": string };

// in: query
export type getPet_Query = { "api_key": string };

// in: cookie
export type getPet_Cookie = { "api_key": string };
```

The apiKey value is also accessible via `$.auth`:
```typescript
export const GET: HTTP_GET = ($) => {
  const key = $.auth["api_key"]; // extracted from the header/query/cookie at runtime
};
```

And API key fields are merged with any explicitly declared parameters of the same kind via intersection:
```typescript
// operation has both a parameter header and the global api_key scheme
export type searchPets_Headers = { "x-request-id": string } & { "api_key": string };
```

### Updated snapshots

The petstore end-to-end snapshot in `generate.test.ts` now includes `_Headers` exports and `auth: { api_key: string }` for all operations that inherit the global `api_key` security scheme, and all operation types include the new `cookie` field.

title: Support multiple OpenAPI specs via multiple --spec flags
body:
Adds support for mounting multiple OpenAPI specs on a single Counterfact server. Each spec is served at its own base path (extracted from `basePath` in OAS2 or `servers[0].url` in OAS3), with duplicate base paths rejected at startup.

## Usage

```sh
counterfact --spec ./api/v1.yaml --spec ./api/v2.yaml ./api
```

- Routes for each spec are served at their respective base paths (e.g. `/api/v1/...`, `/api/v2/...`)
- Swagger UI for each spec is mounted under `/counterfact/swagger/<base-path>`
- Generated code for each spec goes into `<destination>/<slug>/` subdirectories
- If two specs share the same base path, Counterfact prints an error to stderr and exits

## Changes

### `bin/counterfact.js`
- `--spec` now collects multiple values (can be passed more than once); single-spec behavior is unchanged
- `getSpecBasePath()` extracts the URL base path from OAS2 and OAS3 documents
- Single unified `main()` function handles both single and multiple specs — one spec is just an array of size one

### `src/app.ts`
- `setupSpec(config)` — internal helper that initializes registry, dispatcher, transpiler, moduleLoader, and koaMiddleware for a single spec
- `counterfact(configs: Config[])` — accepts an array of configs; a single spec is passed as `[config]`; no separate single/multiple entry points

### `src/server/create-koa-app.ts`
- Added `SpecEntry` interface grouping `{ registry, koaMiddleware, config, contextRegistry }` per spec
- `createKoaApp(entries: SpecEntry[])` — always takes an array; mounts per-spec OpenAPI docs and Swagger UI based on each entry's `routePrefix` (empty prefix preserves the original `/counterfact/swagger/` path for backward compatibility)

### `src/server/openapi-middleware.ts`
- Added optional `servePath` parameter (default: `/counterfact/openapi`) to allow each spec to be served at a distinct URL

title: Version Packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## counterfact@2.4.0

### Minor Changes

-   cb931d6: When multiple wildcard route handlers exist at the same path level (e.g. `/{x}` and `/{y}` as siblings), Counterfact now:
    1.  Logs an error to stderr at load time listing the conflicting wildcard names.
    2.  Returns an HTTP 500 response when a request could be routed to two or more handlers due to the ambiguity.

-   0a3039b: Add support for binary data in responses. Route handlers can now return binary content using the new `binary()` method on the response builder, which accepts a `Buffer` or a base64-encoded string. OpenAPI schemas with `format: "binary"` (v3) or `type: "file"` (v2) now generate `Buffer | string` TypeScript types.

-   d53f4c3: Break REPL out of `counterfact()` and expose it as a callable `startRepl()` on the returned object. This enables programmatic usage (e.g. from Playwright tests) without automatically starting an interactive terminal session.

    ```ts
    import { counterfact } from "counterfact";

    const { contextRegistry, start, startRepl } = await counterfact(config);
    await start(config);

    // Manipulate server state directly from test code:
    const rootContext = contextRegistry.find("/");
    rootContext.passwordResponse = "expired";
    ```

    The CLI (`bin/counterfact.js`) now explicitly calls `startRepl()` when `--repl` is passed, preserving existing behaviour.

-   861c4db: Add route autocomplete to REPL for `client.<method>("...")` patterns.

    When typing `client.get("/p` in the REPL and pressing Tab, the REPL now suggests available routes (e.g. `/pets`, `/pets/{petId}`) derived from the route registry.

    This works for all HTTP methods: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, and `delete`.

-   1e4d5cf: Add chainable `$.response.cookie()` helper for setting response cookies.

    Route handlers can now set one or more cookies without manually building `Set-Cookie` header strings:

    ```ts
    return $.response[200]
      .cookie("sessionId", "abc123", {
        httpOnly: true,
        secure: true,
        sameSite: "lax",
        path: "/",
        maxAge: 3600,
      })
      .cookie("theme", "dark")
      .json({ ok: true });
    ```

    Supported options: `path`, `domain`, `maxAge`, `expires`, `httpOnly`, `secure`, `sameSite`.

### Patch Changes

-   578faab: Fix REPL tab completion for built-in Node.js completions (e.g. `context.<Tab>`).

    The custom route completer previously replaced Node's built-in REPL completer entirely, breaking property completion for objects like `context` and `client`. The completer now delegates to the built-in completer when the input doesn't match the `client.<method>("...")` pattern.

-   76d3103: Updated dependency `json-schema-faker` to `0.6.0`.

-   4229034: Updated dependency `eslint` to `10.0.3`.

-   635071c: Updated dependency `eslint-plugin-jest` to `29.15.1`.

-   ff36c53: Updated dependency `handlebars` to `4.7.9`.

-   9e2b147: Updated dependency `typescript` to `6.0.2`.

-   7f9ce73: Updated dependency `@swc/core` to `1.15.21`.

-   a7a56a2: Updated dependency `eslint` to `10.1.0`.

title: fix(deps): update dependency handlebars to v4.7.9 [security]
body:
This PR contains the following updates: | Package | Change | [Age](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | [Confidence](https://docs.renovatebot.com/merge-confidence/) | |---|---|---|---| | [handlebars](https://handlebarsjs.com/) ([source](https://redirect.github.com/handlebars-lang/handlebars.js)) | [`4.7.8` → `4.7.9`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/handlebars/4.7.8/4.7.9) | ![age](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/age/npm/handlebars/4.7.9?slim=true) | ![confidence](https://developer.mend.io/api/mc/badges/confidence/npm/handlebars/4.7.8/4.7.9?slim=true) | ### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts #### [CVE-2026-33916](https://redirect.github.com/handlebars-lang/handlebars.js/security/advisories/GHSA-2qvq-rjwj-gvw9) ## Summary `resolvePartial()` in the Handlebars runtime resolves partial names via a plain property lookup on `options.partials` without guarding against prototype-chain traversal. When `Object.prototype` has been polluted with a string value whose key matches a partial reference in a template, the polluted string is used as the partial body and rendered **without HTML escaping**, resulting in reflected or stored XSS. ## Description The root cause is in `lib/handlebars/runtime.js` inside `resolvePartial()` and `invokePartial()`: ```javascript // Vulnerable: plain bracket access traverses Object.prototype partial = options.partials[options.name]; ``` `hasOwnProperty` is never checked, so if `Object.prototype` has been seeded with a key whose name matches a partial reference in the template (e.g. `widget`), the lookup succeeds and the polluted string is returned. The runtime emits a prototype-access warning, but the partial is still resolved and its content is inserted into the rendered output unescaped. This contradicts the documented security model and is distinct from CVE-2021-23369 and CVE-2021-23383, which addressed data property access rather than partial template resolution. **Prerequisites for exploitation:** 1. The target application must be vulnerable to prototype pollution (e.g. via `qs`, `minimist`, or any querystring/JSON merge sink). 2. The attacker must know or guess the name of a partial reference used in a template. ## Proof of Concept ```javascript const Handlebars = require('handlebars'); // Step 1: Prototype pollution (via qs, minimist, or another vector) Object.prototype.widget = ''; // Step 2: Normal template that references a partial const template = Handlebars.compile('
Welcome! {{> widget}}
'); // Step 3: Render — XSS payload injected unescaped const output = template({}); // Output:
Welcome!
``` > The runtime prints a prototype access warning claiming "access has been denied," but the partial still resolves and returns the polluted value. ## Workarounds - Apply `Object.freeze(Object.prototype)` early in application startup to prevent prototype pollution. Note: this may break other libraries. - Use the Handlebars runtime-only build (`handlebars/runtime`), which does not compile templates and reduces the attack surface. --- ### Release Notes

title: Invalid example name returns 200 “ok” instead of failing
body:
## Minimal repro

OpenAPI path:

```yaml 
/hello/{name}:
  get:
    parameters:
      - in: path
        name: name
        required: true
        schema:
          type: string
    responses:
      default:
        description: Successful response
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: string
            examples:
              hello-example1:
                value: Hello, example1
              hello-example2:
                value: Hello, example2
```

Route:

```ts
import type { HTTP_GET } from "../../types/paths/hello/{name}.types.js";

export const GET: HTTP_GET = async ($) => {
  return $.response[200].example("hello-example3");
};
```

Steps to reproduce

1. Define the OpenAPI path above.
2. Implement the route above.
3. Send GET /hello/whatever.

## Expected behavior

Counterfact should fail because hello-example3 does not exist.
A 500 error would be acceptable.

## Actual behavior

Counterfact returns:
- status: 200
- body: "ok"

## Notes

The route is requesting an example name that is not defined in the OpenAPI document.
Instead of surfacing that as an error, Counterfact appears to fall back to a successful default response.

It's probably due to a larger issue, that exceptions are swallowed somewhere.

title: Return 500 when `.example()` is called with a name not defined in the OpenAPI spec
body:
`$.response[status].example(name)` silently returned `undefined` body with status 200 when the requested example name didn't exist in any content type — no error surfaced at all.

## Changes

- **`src/server/response-builder.ts`**: After confirming `response.content` exists, check whether the requested example name appears in at least one content type. If not, return a 500 with a descriptive message:
  ```
  The OpenAPI document does not define an example named "hello-example3" for status code 200
  ```
- **`test/server/response-builder.test.ts`**: Add test covering the new 500 error path for an unknown example name.

title: Add chainable `$.response.cookie()` helper for setting response cooki
body:
## Description

Implement a new response helper:

```ts
$.response.cookie(name, value, options?)
```

This helper should allow route handlers to add one or more cookies to the response without manually building `Set-Cookie` header strings.

---

## Example usage

```ts
export const GET = async ($) => {
  return $.response
    .cookie("sessionId", "abc123", {
      httpOnly: true,
      secure: true,
      sameSite: "lax",
      path: "/",
      maxAge: 3600
    })
    .json({ ok: true });
};
```

Multiple cookies should work:

```ts
return $.response
  .cookie("sessionId", "abc123")
  .cookie("theme", "dark")
  .json({ ok: true });
```

---

## Requirements

1. Add a `cookie(name, value, options?)` method to the response builder.  
2. The method must be chainable and return the response builder instance.  
3. Each call must append a new `Set-Cookie` value rather than overwriting prior cookies.  
4. Cookie values must be serialized into valid `Set-Cookie` strings.  
5. This must integrate cleanly with the existing response-building flow.  
6. Do not require route authors to call `.header("Set-Cookie", ...)` manually.  

---

## Supported options

Support these option fields:

```ts
type CookieOptions = {
  domain?: string;
  expires?: Date;
  httpOnly?: boolean;
  maxAge?: number;
  path?: string;
  sameSite?: "lax" | "strict" | "none";
  secure?: boolean;
};
```

---

## Behavior details

- `name` and `value` should be strings.  
- `maxAge` should serialize as `Max-Age=<number>`.  
- `expires` should serialize as `Expires=<UTC string>`.  
- Boolean flags like `HttpOnly` and `Secure` should be included only when true.  
- `sameSite` should serialize as `SameSite=Lax`, `SameSite=Strict`, or `SameSite=None`.  
- `path` and `domain` should serialize normally when provided.  
- Preserve the order of cookie attributes in a consistent way.  
- Multiple cookies must survive all the way to the final HTTP response as distinct `Set-Cookie` values.  

---

## Implementation guidance

- Reuse existing response header infrastructure where practical.  
- If headers are currently stored as single values, update the implementation so `Set-Cookie` can support multiple values safely without breaking other headers.  
- Prefer a small internal serializer function over adding a large dependency.  
- Keep the change focused. Do not add cookie parsing or request-side cookie APIs in this issue.  

---

## Suggested steps

1. Find the response builder implementation.  
2. Add a `cookie()` method.  
3. Add a small internal cookie serialization utility.  
4. Ensure response headers can carry multiple `Set-Cookie` values.  
5. Add or update tests for:
   - one cookie  
   - multiple cookies  
   - all supported options  
   - chaining with existing response helpers like `.json()`  

---

## Acceptance criteria

- `$.response.cookie("a", "1")` adds one valid `Set-Cookie` header.  
- Multiple `.cookie()` calls produce multiple `Set-Cookie` header values.  
- `.cookie()` can be chained before or after `.json()`, `.example()`, or other response helpers.  
- Existing response behavior continues to work.  
- Tests pass.  

---

## Out of scope

- `$.cookies`  
- `clearCookie()`  
- OpenAPI cookie metadata  
- automatic auth or session features  

---

## Implementation notes for Copilot

Make the smallest clean change that fits the current architecture.  
Prefer extending existing response-builder patterns over introducing a parallel mechanism.  
Include tests.
Include documentation.
Include a changeset.

title: Add `$.cookie` helper for reading request cookies (type-safe, spec-aware)
body:
## Description

Implement a request helper for accessing cookies:

```ts
$.cookie(name)
```

This helper should provide a clean, type-safe way to read cookies from the incoming request without manually parsing the `Cookie` header.

This mirrors `$.user` (basic auth) and aligns with Counterfact’s goal of providing high-level, intention-based APIs instead of raw HTTP handling.

---

## Example usage

```ts
export const GET = async ($) => {
  const sessionId = $.cookie("sessionId");

  return $.response.json({ sessionId });
};
```

With optional fallback:

```ts
const theme = $.cookie("theme") ?? "light";
```

---

## Requirements

1. Add a `cookie(name)` method on the request context `$`.
2. The method must return:
   - `string | undefined` (undefined if cookie is not present)
3. Must correctly parse the `Cookie` header from the request.
4. Must handle multiple cookies in a single header.
5. Must be safe and not throw on malformed cookie headers.
6. Must not require users to manually access headers.

---

## Behavior details

- Parse the `Cookie` header according to standard format:
  - `"key1=value1; key2=value2"`
- Trim whitespace around keys and values.
- Return the decoded value (URL-decoding if applicable).
- If the cookie is not present, return `undefined`.
- If duplicate cookie names exist, return the first occurrence.

---

## Type safety (Phase 1)

Basic API:

```ts
cookie(name: string): string | undefined;
```

---

## Type safety (Phase 2 - spec-aware)

If the OpenAPI spec defines cookies using:

- `in: cookie` parameters
- or `apiKey` security schemes with `in: cookie`

then generate a union type of known cookie names:

```ts
type RequestCookieName = "sessionId" | "theme";
```

And narrow the API:

```ts
cookie(name: RequestCookieName): string | undefined;
```

Fallback to `string` if the spec is not specific enough.

---

## Implementation guidance

- Reuse existing request header access if available.
- Implement a small internal cookie parser (avoid heavy dependencies).
- Cache parsed cookies per request to avoid repeated parsing.
- Keep parsing logic isolated and testable.

---

## Suggested steps

1. Locate request context (`$`) implementation.
2. Add `cookie(name)` method.
3. Implement cookie parsing utility.
4. Cache parsed result on first access.
5. Add tests for:
   - single cookie
   - multiple cookies
   - missing cookie
   - malformed header
   - whitespace handling
   - URL-encoded values

---

## Acceptance criteria

- `$.cookie("a")` returns the correct value when present.
- Returns `undefined` when cookie is missing.
- Handles multiple cookies correctly.
- Does not throw on malformed input.
- Works alongside existing request helpers.
- Tests pass.

---

## Out of scope

- Setting cookies (`$.response.cookie()` is handled separately)
- Cookie signing or encryption
- Automatic auth/session handling
- OpenAPI response cookie support

---

## Implementation notes for Copilot

Make the smallest clean change that fits the current architecture.  
Prefer extending existing request context patterns.  
Cache parsed cookies for efficiency.  
Include tests.

title: Support Multiple API Versions
body:
Possibly related to #1572 . We have consumers of Counterfact that are supporting versioned APIs. Each version has its own Spec file but technically the same `basePath`. Actually OpenApi 3 does away with the `basePath` preferring the `servers` collection. So we can't rely on `basePath` to distinguish specs. Should we combine these two issues? Technically this one is slightly different in that we need to support multiple specs base on the version.

The problem is there isn't a single way to denote variant versions of a spec. Read this discussion here: 
https://www.userosetta.com/blog/simplify-api-versioning-with-openapi

There is the `info.version` field in the spec header, but the stated purpose of that field isn't specifically to version the APIs so much as to version changes to the document. However, our consumers use that very field to denote the `v1`, `v2`, `v3`, etc versions. And the above article suggests using that header field is a perfectly valid way to distinguish versions.

Let's discuss the best path to implement this. I think it is reasonable to use the `version` field, but do we also infer the version from the `servers` collection as some documentation suggests?

In any case, it seems that if we load multiple specs that are variants, we need to build the types indedepently so that even if each spec has the same component name for a model we store it in a versioned path so that each model variant exists to be available as a type. So a `v1` and `v2` set of specs might have a component named `PetModel` live in two potential import paths:

`/components/schemas/v1/PetModel`
`/components/schemas/v2/PetModel`

title: Add route autocomplete to REPL for client.<method>("...")
body:
## Summary

Enhance the Counterfact REPL to support autocomplete for API routes when using the `client` helper.

When a user types:

```ts
client.get("
```

and presses Tab, the REPL should suggest available routes derived from the route registry.

This improves discoverability and makes the REPL feel like an interactive API explorer.

## Problem

Currently, the REPL only supports basic Node.js tab completion based on runtime objects.

It does not support:
- autocompleting string arguments
- suggesting valid API routes
- helping users discover available endpoints

This makes the REPL less useful, especially for new users who do not know the available routes.

## Expected Behavior

When typing in the REPL:

```ts
client.get("/p
```

Pressing Tab should suggest matching routes such as:

```ts
"/pets"
"/pets/{petId}"
```

This should work for all HTTP methods:

- `client.get(...)`
- `client.post(...)`
- `client.put(...)`
- `client.patch(...)`
- `client.delete(...)`

## Implementation Approach

Use the `completer` option from Node's `repl` module.

Reference:
https://nodejs.org/api/repl.html#replstartoptions

### Step 1: Inject the registry into `startRepl`

Update the `startRepl()` signature so it receives the registry object.

It currently receives `contextRegistry`, `config`, and `print`.

It should also receive `registry`, since the paths live under `registry.routes`.

Example:

```ts
startRepl(contextRegistry, registry, config, print)
```

### Step 2: Add a completer

Update `repl.start()` in `startRepl()`:

```ts
const replServer = repl.start({
  prompt: "⬣> ",
  completer: createCompleter(registry),
});
```

### Step 3: Implement `createCompleter`

Create a function that:

1. Detects when the user is typing inside:
   - `client.get("...`
   - `client.post("...`
   - `client.put("...`
   - `client.patch("...`
   - `client.delete("...`

2. Extracts the partially typed route

3. Reads all available paths from `registry.routes`

4. Returns matching routes

Example:

```ts
function createCompleter(registry: Registry) {
  const routes = Object.keys(registry.routes);

  return (line: string) => {
    const match = line.match(
      /client\.(get|post|put|patch|delete)\("([^"]*)$/u,
    );

    if (!match) {
      return [[], line];
    }

    const partial = match[2];

    const matches = routes.filter((route) => route.startsWith(partial));

    return [matches, partial];
  };
}
```

### Step 4: Preserve existing REPL behavior

Make sure this does not break:
- `.proxy`
- `.counterfact`
- existing object/property completion where possible

If the current input does not match a supported `client.<method>("...")` pattern, the REPL should fall back cleanly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Typing `client.get("` and pressing Tab shows route suggestions
- Partial matches filter correctly using prefix matching
- Works for:
  - `client.get(...)`
  - `client.post(...)`
  - `client.put(...)`
  - `client.patch(...)`
  - `client.delete(...)`
- Uses `registry.routes` as the source of truth
- `startRepl()` is updated to accept the registry object
- Existing REPL commands still work
- Non-matching input does not break normal REPL behavior

title: Fix REPL tab completion broken by custom completer overriding Node's built-in
body:
The custom `client.<method>("...")` completer replaced Node's built-in REPL completer entirely, so `context.<Tab>` and all other built-in property completions stopped working.

## Summary

The fix converts the completer to async and threads the built-in REPL completer through as a fallback:

```ts
// Before: custom completer passed at startup, replaces built-in
const replServer = repl.start({ completer: createCompleter(registry), prompt: "⬣> " });

// After: capture built-in first, then wrap it
const replServer = repl.start({ prompt: "⬣> " });
const builtinCompleter = replServer.completer as (line: string, callback: CompleterCallback) => void;
// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any
(replServer as any).completer = createCompleter(registry, builtinCompleter);
```

`createCompleter` now accepts an optional async `fallback` and returns an `AsyncCompleter`. When input doesn't match the `client.<method>("...")` pattern, it delegates to the fallback instead of returning empty completions.

`@types/node` marks `REPLServer.completer` as readonly, but Node.js sets it as a plain writable instance property in the constructor. The built-in completer is only available after `repl.start()` returns, so it cannot be passed to `repl.start()` directly — we must capture it from the returned instance and replace it with our wrapper via `as any`.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

REPL tab completion for `context.<Tab>` and all other built-in property completions was broken because the custom `client.<method>("...")` completer replaced Node's built-in REPL completer entirely when passed to `repl.start()`.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Typing `context.` in the REPL and pressing Tab shows property completions (e.g. `context.loadContext`, etc.)
- [x] Typing `client.get("/p` and pressing Tab still suggests matching routes (e.g. `/pets`, `/pets/{petId}`)
- [x] Typing a partial variable name (e.g. `con`) and pressing Tab completes to `context`
- [x] Typing `client.` and pressing Tab shows method completions from the built-in completer
- [x] Pressing Tab on an empty line or unrelated expression does not throw or produce an error

## Tasks

- Changed `createCompleter` signature to accept an optional async `fallback` completer and return `AsyncCompleter` (callback-based)
- In `startRepl`, start REPL without a custom completer, capture `replServer.completer` (the built-in), then assign `createCompleter(registry, builtinCompleter)` via `(replServer as any).completer = ...` to bypass the readonly TypeScript constraint
- Exported `CompleterCallback` type for test reuse
- Updated all autocomplete tests to use the async callback style via a `callCompleter` helper
- Added a test verifying the fallback is invoked for non-matching input
- Added changeset (`patch`)
- Ran `eslint --fix` to correct formatting
