title: Tell Copilot to use TDD
body:
Here are some new instructions. Integrate them into copilot-instructions.md and remove any existing instructions that would be redundant. 

## Test-driven workflow

When implementing a change, work in a test-first or test-guided way whenever practical.

### Default workflow

1. Understand the requested behavior before changing code.
2. Identify the smallest observable behavior that proves the change works.
3. Add or update automated tests for that behavior first.
4. Run the relevant tests and confirm they fail for the expected reason when feasible.
5. Implement the smallest code change needed to make the tests pass.
6. Refactor only after the tests are green.
7. Run all relevant tests again before finishing.

### Expectations

- Prefer adding tests at the level that best captures user-visible behavior.
- Do not change tests merely to accommodate broken behavior unless the requested behavior has changed.
- Do not remove tests without explaining why.
- Avoid over-mocking. Prefer realistic behavior and real integration boundaries where practical.
- Keep tests readable. A test should make it obvious what behavior is expected.
- Cover at least:
  - the main success path
  - one meaningful edge case
  - one regression risk when applicable

### When to add tests

Add or update tests for:
- bug fixes
- new features
- refactors that could change behavior
- generated code, when generation behavior is being changed
- any change that affects external contracts, APIs, schemas, or CLI behavior

### When tests are hard to add

If a test is difficult to write:
1. Do not skip testing silently.
2. Explain why the code is hard to test.
3. Improve the design if possible to make testing easier.
4. If automated coverage is still impractical, provide clear manual verification steps.

### Definition of done

A change is not complete until:
- the relevant tests exist
- the relevant tests pass
- the implementation matches the requested behavior
- manual verification steps are included when needed

### Manual acceptance tests

For every pull request, include a section titled:

Manual acceptance tests

Under that section, provide 3 to 6 unchecked checkboxes describing observable behaviors a human can verify manually. These should include:
- the primary success case
- at least one edge case
- at least one regression check

Example:

- [ ] Creating a pet with a valid payload returns 201
- [ ] Creating a pet with a missing required field returns 400
- [ ] Existing pet lookup behavior still works after the change

### Decision rule

When choosing between:
- writing more production code
- tightening tests
- simplifying design

prefer the option that improves feedback quality and reduces ambiguity.

If you want, I can also give you a version tailored specifically for Counterfact.

title: Add CI workflow to create GitHub issues from proposed issue files + update copilot-instructions.md
body:
## Title
Add CI workflow to create sub-issues from Markdown proposal files and move issue-authoring instructions into a dedicated file

## Summary

We want a safe, reviewable workflow for issue creation.

Instead of allowing Copilot to create GitHub issues directly, we will:

1. Allow Copilot to propose issues as Markdown files in the repo
2. Review those files in a pull request
3. Use a GitHub Action to create real GitHub issues after merge
4. Make each created issue a sub-issue of the issue Copilot is currently implementing
5. Delete the proposal files after successful creation, following the general pattern used by Changesets
6. Move issue-authoring guidance into a dedicated instructions file referenced by `copilot-instructions.md`

This keeps credentials out of the agent runtime, preserves human review, and supports hierarchical planning.

## Requirements

### 1. Proposed issue file location

Create a convention for issue proposal files, for example:

```text
.github/issue-proposals/*.md
```

Each file represents one proposed GitHub issue.

Do not use `.github/issues/`, since that can be confused with GitHub issue templates.

### 2. File format

Use Markdown files with YAML front matter for metadata.

Example:

```md
---
title: Add JSDocs to generated types
parentIssue: 1234
labels:
  - enhancement
  - generator
assignees: []
milestone:
---

Generate JSDoc comments for emitted TypeScript types using metadata from the OpenAPI spec.

## Acceptance criteria

- Description fields map to JSDoc where available
- Parameter and schema docs are preserved
- Generated output remains valid TypeScript
```

Rules:

- Front matter is required
- `title` is required
- Body content after the front matter becomes the GitHub issue body
- `labels`, `assignees`, and `milestone` are optional
- `parentIssue` should be included in front matter by Copilot, but CI should not require it

### 3. Parent issue / sub-issue behavior

Each created issue must be created as a sub-issue of the issue the agent is currently implementing.

Preferred convention:
- include an explicit `parentIssue` field in front matter so the relationship is visible and auditable in the file itself

However, the CI workflow must not require `parentIssue` to be present in the proposal file.

Instead, the workflow should determine the parent issue using repository context, such as the issue associated with the pull request or branch being merged. If `parentIssue` is present, the workflow may use it as a hint or validation aid, but the source of truth should be the workflow’s derived parent context.

If the workflow cannot determine the parent issue for a proposal file, fail processing for that file and do not delete it.

### 4. GitHub Action

Create a workflow at:

```text
.github/workflows/create-issues.yml
```

Behavior:

- Trigger on push to `main` when files under `.github/issue-proposals/*.md` change
- For each Markdown proposal file:
  - Parse front matter
  - Validate required fields
  - Use the Markdown body as the issue body
  - Determine the parent issue from repository context
  - Create a GitHub issue
  - Associate it as a sub-issue of the resolved parent issue
  - Apply labels if provided
  - Apply assignees if provided
  - Apply milestone if provided and resolvable

Use the repository token:

```yaml
GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

Use the GitHub API or `gh` CLI, whichever is simpler and more reliable for sub-issue creation.

### 5. Cleanup after creation

After a proposal file is successfully converted into a GitHub issue, delete the file from `.github/issue-proposals/`.

This should follow the general pattern of Changesets:

- proposal files live in the repo while under review
- merge to `main` triggers processing
- successful processing removes the consumed file

Implementation note:
- the workflow should commit the deletion back to the repository after successful issue creation

### 6. Failure behavior

If issue creation fails for any file:

- do not delete that file
- fail the workflow
- leave the file in place so it can be retried after the problem is fixed

### 7. Validation

Fail the workflow if:

- front matter is missing
- front matter is invalid YAML
- `title` is missing or empty
- body content is empty
- the workflow cannot determine a parent issue from repository context

Do not fail merely because `parentIssue` is missing from front matter.

### 8. Move instructions into a dedicated file

Create a dedicated instructions file for issue proposal authoring, for example:

```text
.github/instructions/issue-proposals.instructions.md
```

This file should define:

• where issue proposal files go  
• the required Markdown + front matter format  
• required and optional fields  
• that proposals are intended to become sub-issues of the current parent issue  
• that Copilot should include `parentIssue` in front matter when possible, even though CI does not require it  
• that Copilot must never attempt direct issue creation via API or browser automation  
• expectations for issue quality, including context and acceptance criteria

Then update `copilot-instructions.md` so it references this file rather than embedding all of the issue-authoring rules inline.

The goal is to keep `copilot-instructions.md` concise and make the issue workflow reusable and easier to maintain.

### 9. Update copilot-instructions.md

Update `copilot-instructions.md` so Copilot:

- references the dedicated issue proposal instructions file
- never attempts to create issues directly via API or browser automation
- always proposes issues as Markdown files under `.github/issue-proposals/`
- uses YAML front matter for metadata
- includes `parentIssue` when possible
- writes clear issue bodies with:
  - summary/context
  - motivation
  - acceptance criteria

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Markdown-based issue proposal format exists under `.github/issue-proposals/*.md`
- [ ] Front matter is parsed and validated
- [ ] Workflow exists at `.github/workflows/create-issues.yml`
- [ ] Workflow creates GitHub issues from valid proposal files
- [ ] Workflow determines the parent issue from repository context
- [ ] Workflow associates each created issue as a sub-issue of the resolved parent issue
- [ ] Workflow applies labels and assignees when provided
- [ ] Workflow attempts milestone assignment when provided
- [ ] Successfully processed proposal files are deleted automatically
- [ ] Failed proposal files remain in the repo
- [ ] Dedicated issue-authoring instructions file exists
- [ ] `copilot-instructions.md` references that file
- [ ] Copilot no longer attempts direct issue creation

## Example proposal file

```md
---
title: Add JSDocs to generated types
parentIssue: 1234
labels:
  - enhancement
  - generator
assignees: []
milestone:
---

Generate JSDoc comments for emitted TypeScript types using metadata from the OpenAPI spec.

## Acceptance criteria

- Description fields map to JSDoc where available
- Parameter and schema docs are preserved
- Generated output remains valid TypeScript
```

## Notes for implementation

- Prefer a simple implementation over a clever one
- Keep dependencies minimal
- A small script checked into the repo is fine if it makes the workflow easier to read and test
- The workflow should be able to process multiple issue files in one run
- The commit that deletes processed files should be clearly attributable to the workflow
- The sub-issue linkage should be implemented in a way that is robust and testable
- `parentIssue` in front matter is for clarity and authoring guidance, not as a hard CI requirement

## Why this matters

- Keeps credentials out of agent runtime
- Makes issue creation reviewable through pull requests
- Preserves a clean audit trail
- Supports parent/child planning
- Keeps the repo tidy by removing consumed proposal files
- Keeps Copilot guidance modular and maintainable

title: OpenAPI 3.2 — Opportunities for Counterfact
body:
## Objective

Break this issue down into subtasks. Do not write any code. 

## Summary 

OpenAPI 3.2 was released in early 2025. This issue identifies changes in the specification and maps each one to a concrete opportunity for Counterfact to adopt it so that Counterfact can be listed as an OpenAPI 3.2 early adopter on [OpenAPI.tools](https://openapi.tools).

The opportunities are grouped by theme and rated by **impact** (how much value it adds to Counterfact users) and **effort** (how much work is required to implement it).

---

## 1. New and Extended HTTP Methods

### 1a. Native `QUERY` method

OpenAPI 3.2 formally adds `query` as a first-class HTTP method alongside `get`, `post`, `put`, `delete`, `options`, `head`, `patch`, and `trace`. The [QUERY method](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-httpbis-safe-method-w-body-02.html) is safe and idempotent but allows a request body, making it useful for complex search/filter operations.

**Current state:** `HttpMethods` in `src/server/registry.ts` and `HTTP_METHODS` in `src/migrate/update-route-types.ts` do not include `QUERY`. The Koa layer, dispatcher, and migration helper would all need updating.

**Opportunity:** Add `"QUERY"` to `HttpMethods`, `ALL_HTTP_METHODS`, and the migration helper's `HTTP_METHODS` list. The code generator already iterates over all keys in a path definition, so generation would work automatically once the server recognises the method.

**Impact:** Medium — Enables mock servers for APIs that use the QUERY method  
**Effort:** Low — Small, mechanical additions to a handful of files

### 1b. Arbitrary methods via `additionalOperations`

For HTTP methods that do not have a dedicated field in the Path Item Object (e.g. `LINK`, `UNLINK`, `LOCK`), OpenAPI 3.2 introduces an `additionalOperations` key. Values are Operation Objects keyed by the method name in its correct capitalisation.

**Current state:** The generator in `src/typescript-generator/generate.ts` iterates over all top-level keys in each path item, so keys like `get`, `post`, etc. are processed automatically. However, `additionalOperations` is a *nested* object and would not be unwrapped by the current loop; those operations would be silently ignored.

**Opportunity:** Detect the `additionalOperations` key during code generation and flatten its entries into the same processing loop. The server layer would also need to forward requests with custom method names to the matching handler.

**Impact:** Low–Medium — Niche use cases but required for full 3.2 compliance  
**Effort:** Medium — Requires changes to the generator loop and the Koa/dispatcher layer

---

## 2. Streaming and Sequential Media Types

OpenAPI 3.2 introduces first-class support for streaming responses via sequential media types such as `text/event-stream` (Server-Sent Events), `multipart/mixed`, `application/jsonl`, and `application/json-seq`. A new `itemSchema` field in the Media Type Object describes the schema of each individual item in the stream, while responses are conceptually treated as arrays of schema instances.

**Current state:** Counterfact generates typed response builders and can return example data from the spec, but has no concept of streaming or server-sent events. The `text/event-stream` content type is not specially handled.

**Opportunity:**

- Recognise `itemSchema` in `src/typescript-generator/schema-type-coder.ts` / `src/typescript-generator/response-type-coder.ts` and generate `Array<T>` types for it.
- In the server layer, when a request accepts `text/event-stream`, send an SSE-formatted response (using Node.js streams) instead of a one-shot JSON body.
- Expose a helper on the `$` argument (similar to `$.proxy`) that allows route handlers to push events to a stream.

**Impact:** High — SSE is widely used in modern APIs (AI/LLM streaming, real-time dashboards)  
**Effort:** High — Requires new server streaming infrastructure and type-generation changes

---

## 3. `querystring` Parameter Location

OpenAPI 3.2 adds `querystring` as a new value for the `in` field of a Parameter Object. Unlike the existing `query` (which targets a single named query parameter), `querystring` treats the entire query string as a single field and allows it to be parsed with a schema, similar to how `requestBody` works for request bodies.

**Current state:** `src/typescript-generator/parameters-type-coder.ts` generates typed objects for `query`, `path`, `header`, and `cookie` parameters. A `querystring` parameter would be ignored.

**Opportunity:** Handle `in: querystring` in `ParametersTypeCoder` and in the dispatcher's parameter-extraction logic. Generate a typed `querystring` property on the `$` argument.

**Impact:** Medium — Simplifies complex query-string APIs (e.g. OData, OpenSearch)  
**Effort:** Medium — Requires changes to both the type generator and the server dispatcher

---

## 4. Example Object — `dataValue` and `serializedValue`

The Example Object gains two new fields:

- `dataValue` — the example expressed as a structured (parsed) value, analogous to the existing `value` field.
- `serializedValue` — the example as it would appear on the wire, as a string.

The existing `externalValue` is now explicitly documented as a serialized value.

**Current state:** Counterfact's random-response logic reads the `value` field from Example Objects when returning example responses.

**Opportunity:**

- Prefer `dataValue` over `value` when generating example responses so that structured data is used correctly.
- Optionally support `serializedValue` for content types where the wire format differs from the parsed form (e.g. `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`).

**Impact:** Medium — Improves correctness of example responses for APIs that use the new fields  
**Effort:** Low — A small change in the response-building / example-selection logic

---

## 5. Discriminator Improvements

### 5a. Optional `propertyName`

The `discriminator.propertyName` field is now optional. When absent, a `defaultMapping` (see below) must be provided.

**Current state:** `SchemaTypeCoder.writeGroup()` relies on `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` without inspecting the `discriminator` object; `propertyName` being absent would not cause an error but the generated union type would be unchanged.

**Opportunity:** No immediate breaking change; ensure that the absence of `propertyName` does not cause a runtime error during type generation.

**Impact:** Low  
**Effort:** Low — Defensive null-check only

### 5b. `defaultMapping`

A new `defaultMapping` field on the Discriminator Object specifies which schema to use when `propertyName` is absent or the value is not found in `mapping`.

**Opportunity:** Use `defaultMapping` in `SchemaTypeCoder` to emit a more accurate union type when generating TypeScript, including the default variant.

**Impact:** Low–Medium — Improves accuracy of generated types for polymorphic schemas  
**Effort:** Low — Small addition to `SchemaTypeCoder.writeGroup()`

---

## 6. Tag Enhancements

Tags gain three new fields:

- `summary` — a short title for the tag, used in lists.
- `parent` — points to a parent tag to support nested grouping.
- `kind` — classifies the tag (e.g. `nav`, `audience`). A [public registry](https://spec.openapis.org/registry/tag-kind/index.html) defines conventional values.

**Current state:** Counterfact does not currently process or display tag metadata.

**Opportunity:** The built-in dashboard / Swagger UI page (`src/client/`) could use `summary`, `parent`, and `kind` to render a hierarchical navigation tree, grouping operations by nested tags. This would be particularly valuable for large APIs.

**Impact:** Medium — Improves discoverability in the built-in UI for large APIs  
**Effort:** Medium — Frontend work in the Handlebars/Vue layer

---

## 7. Response Object Changes

### 7a. `description` is now optional

Previously, the Response Object required `description`. In 3.2 it is optional.

**Current state:** The generator does not validate or use `description`. Missing descriptions would not cause an error in the current code.

**Opportunity:** No code changes needed; confirm in the test suite that an operation with responses that have no `description` is handled gracefully.

**Impact:** Low — Correctness / robustness improvement  
**Effort:** Very Low — Add a test case

### 7b. New `summary` field on responses

A short `summary` field is now supported alongside `description` on Response Objects.

**Opportunity:** Surface `summary` in the built-in API-testing UI (`src/client/api-tester.html.hbs`) as a tooltip or label when listing available response codes.

**Impact:** Low — Minor UX improvement  
**Effort:** Low

---

## 8. Security Scheme Updates

### 8a. OAuth2 Device Authorization flow

The OAuth2 Security Scheme Flows Object gains a `deviceAuthorization` entry with a `deviceAuthorizationUrl` field (per [RFC 8628](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8628)).

**Current state:** Counterfact's `OperationTypeCoder` checks for `type === "http" && scheme === "basic"` to determine the `user` type on the `$` argument. Other flows are not specially handled.

**Opportunity:** Recognise `deviceAuthorization` flow in `OperationTypeCoder` so that the generated handler type includes the correct credential shape for device-flow tokens.

**Impact:** Low–Medium — Niche but growing use case (CLI tools, smart TVs)  
**Effort:** Low

### 8b. `oauth2MetadataUrl`

A new top-level field on the OAuth2 Security Scheme provides the URL of the authorisation server's metadata document (per [RFC 8414](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414)).

**Opportunity:** Display this URL in the built-in dashboard to help developers configure OAuth2 clients against the mock server.

**Impact:** Low  
**Effort:** Low

### 8c. `deprecated` on security schemes

Security schemes can now be marked `deprecated: true`.

**Opportunity:** Emit a TypeScript `@deprecated` JSDoc comment in the generated handler types when the security scheme used by an operation is deprecated.

**Impact:** Low — Surfaces specification intent to developers as a compiler warning  
**Effort:** Low

---

## 9. `$self` — Document Identity and URL Resolution

A new top-level `$self` field allows an OpenAPI document to declare its own canonical URI, which is used as the base when resolving relative `$ref` values.

**Current state:** Counterfact uses `@apidevtools/json-schema-ref-parser` for bundling, which already handles base-URI resolution. The `$self` field would be passed through.

**Opportunity:** Ensure that the spec loader in `src/typescript-generator/specification.ts` and `src/server/openapi-middleware.ts` does not strip or misinterpret `$self` when bundling. Add a test with a spec that uses `$self` to verify correct `$ref` resolution.

**Impact:** Low — Mainly a correctness/robustness guarantee  
**Effort:** Very Low — Likely already works; add a regression test

---

## 10. `mediaTypes` Component

A new `mediaTypes` key is supported under `components` to allow reuse of Media Type Objects (similar to how `schemas`, `responses`, `parameters`, and `examples` are reused today).

**Current state:** `src/typescript-generator/generate.ts` only reads `#/paths` and `#/components/securitySchemes`. Other component types are resolved via `$ref` by the bundler.

**Opportunity:** Ensure that `$ref` values pointing to `#/components/mediaTypes/...` are resolved correctly at both code-generation time and at runtime. The bundler likely handles this automatically; add a test to confirm.

**Impact:** Low — Reuse of media type definitions is a DX improvement for API designers  
**Effort:** Very Low — Likely already works via `$ref` bundling; add a test

---

## 11. XML `nodeType` Field

A new `nodeType` field on the XML Object maps a schema to an XML node type: `element`, `attribute`, `text`, `cdata`, or `none`. `attribute: true` is deprecated in favour of `nodeType: attribute`, and `wrapped: true` is deprecated in favour of `nodeType: element`.

**Current state:** Counterfact has a `src/server/json-to-xml.ts` helper for XML serialisation, but it is not clear how much of the XML Object is currently supported.

**Opportunity:** Update `json-to-xml.ts` to understand `nodeType` and treat the deprecated `attribute: true` / `wrapped: true` fields as synonyms during the transition period.

**Impact:** Low — Relevant only to XML-based APIs  
**Effort:** Medium — Requires understanding and updating the XML serialisation logic

---

## 12. Server Object `name` Field

The Server Object gains a `name` field alongside the existing `description`, `url`, and `variables` fields.

**Current state:** `src/server/openapi-middleware.ts` injects a `Counterfact` server entry with only `description` and `url`.

**Opportunity:** Set `name: "Counterfact"` in the injected server entry so that tools that display `name` (including OpenAPI 3.2-aware UIs) render it correctly.

**Impact:** Low — Minor UX improvement in Swagger UI and similar tools  
**Effort:** Very Low — One-line change in `openapi-middleware.ts`

---

## 13. JSON Schema Alignment

OpenAPI 3.2 updates its embedded JSON Schema reference to [draft-bhutton-json-schema-01](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-bhutton-json-schema-01.html) and [draft-bhutton-json-schema-validation-01](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-bhutton-json-schema-validation-01.html).

**Current state:** Counterfact uses `json-schema-faker` for generating random values from schemas. The library's supported draft determines what schema keywords are available.

**Opportunity:** Verify that `json-schema-faker` supports the keywords introduced in `draft-bhutton-json-schema-01` (notably the revised `unevaluatedProperties`, `unevaluatedItems`, and `prefixItems`). Upgrade the library or add workarounds as necessary.

**Impact:** Medium — Affects correctness of random response generation  
**Effort:** Low–Medium — Depends on the library's current support level

---

## Summary Table

| Opportunity | Impact | Effort | Files Affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1a. `QUERY` HTTP method | Medium | Low | `registry.ts`, `update-route-types.ts`, `koa-middleware.ts` |
| 1b. `additionalOperations` | Low–Medium | Medium | `generate.ts`, `dispatcher.ts`, `registry.ts` |
| 2. Streaming / SSE (`itemSchema`) | High | High | `response-type-coder.ts`, `schema-type-coder.ts`, `koa-middleware.ts`, new streaming helper |
| 3. `querystring` parameter | Medium | Medium | `parameters-type-coder.ts`, `dispatcher.ts` |
| 4. `dataValue`/`serializedValue` examples | Medium | Low | Response/example selection logic |
| 5a. Optional discriminator `propertyName` | Low | Low | `schema-type-coder.ts` |
| 5b. Discriminator `defaultMapping` | Low–Medium | Low | `schema-type-coder.ts` |
| 6. Tag `summary`/`parent`/`kind` | Medium | Medium | `src/client/` templates |
| 7a. Optional response `description` | Low | Very Low | Test only |
| 7b. Response `summary` | Low | Low | `src/client/api-tester.html.hbs` |
| 8a. OAuth2 Device Authorization flow | Low–Medium | Low | `operation-type-coder.ts` |
| 8b. `oauth2MetadataUrl` | Low | Low | `src/client/` templates |
| 8c. `deprecated` security scheme | Low | Low | `operation-type-coder.ts` |
| 9. `$self` document identity | Low | Very Low | Test only |
| 10. `mediaTypes` component | Low | Very Low | Test only |
| 11. XML `nodeType` | Low | Medium | `json-to-xml.ts` |
| 12. Server `name` field | Low | Very Low | `openapi-middleware.ts` |
| 13. JSON Schema alignment | Medium | Low–Medium | `json-schema-faker` usage |

---

## Recommended Starting Points

If the goal is to be listed as an **early adopter** with minimal investment, the highest-return items are:

1. **`QUERY` HTTP method (1a)** — High visibility, low effort, clearly demonstrates 3.2 awareness.
2. **`dataValue`/`serializedValue` examples (4)** — Simple change with user-visible impact on example responses.
3. **Server `name` field (12)** — Trivial change that shows up in every OpenAPI-aware UI.
4. **Streaming / SSE (2)** — High user demand; worth investing in even though it requires more work.
5. **`querystring` parameter (3)** — Useful for complex search/filter APIs; moderate effort.

---

title: Version Packages
body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## counterfact@2.6.0

### Minor Changes

-   3b0334a: Add JSDoc comment generation for types from OpenAPI metadata

    Generated TypeScript types now include inline JSDoc comments derived from the OpenAPI spec:

    -   Schema-level JSDoc from `description`/`summary`
    -   Property-level JSDoc including `description`, `@example`, `@default`, `@format`, and `@deprecated`
    -   Operation-level JSDoc from operation `summary`/`description`

    This improves IDE hover documentation and AI-assisted development workflows.

-   a3b24f0: Add request validation against the OpenAPI spec. Incoming requests are now validated by default — missing required query parameters, missing required headers, and request bodies that do not match the declared schema all result in a 400 response with a descriptive error message. Validation can be disabled with the `--no-validate-request` CLI flag.

-   3c5c284: Add lightweight telemetry using PostHog to track usage of Counterfact. Fires a single `counterfact_started` event on startup. Telemetry is disabled by default before May 1, 2026, disabled in CI, and can be controlled with the `COUNTERFACT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` environment variable. A one-time warning is shown before the rollout date.

-   6c9e30f: Add REPL-native request builder (`route()`) with fluent API, OpenAPI introspection, and autocomplete support.

    The new `route()` function is available in the REPL and allows users to discover, construct, and execute API requests interactively:

    ```js
    const pet = route("/pet/{petId}").method("get").path({ petId: 1 });

    await pet.send();
    ```

    Key capabilities:

    -   Fluent, immutable builder API (`.method()`, `.path()`, `.query()`, `.headers()`, `.body()`)
    -   OpenAPI-backed introspection via `.help()`, `.ready()`, and `.missing()`
    -   Actionable feedback when required parameters are absent
    -   Custom REPL display showing parameter status
    -   Autocomplete for `route("` in addition to existing `client.*` patterns

### Patch Changes

-   7a89d27: Refactor internal plain objects to Maps where appropriate:
    -   `Directory.directories` and `Directory.files` in `module-tree.ts` are now `Map<string, Directory>` and `Map<string, File>`
    -   `ParameterTypes` inner types in `dispatcher.ts` are now `Map<string, string>`
    -   `castParameters` in `registry.ts` now accepts `Map<string, string>` for parameter types
-   5b7d8b3: Improve error messages for malformed or missing OpenAPI specs. Instead of showing a JavaScript stack trace, Counterfact now displays a clear, actionable message that includes the spec path and the underlying reason for the failure.
-   ff2ba80: Auto-detect TypeScript native runtime support (tsx, ts-node, node --experimental-strip-types) instead of requiring a --use-tsx flag

title: Bug: Tools.accepts() ignores lowercase 'accept' header — always returns true in production
body:
`Tools.accepts()` reads `this.headers.Accept` (capital A). Node.js normalises all incoming HTTP header names to **lowercase**, so when a real HTTP request is processed via Koa the header is stored under `accept` (lowercase). `this.headers.Accept` is therefore always `undefined` in production.

Because `undefined` triggers the early-return guard `if (acceptHeader === "" || acceptHeader === undefined) { return true; }`, the method unconditionally returns `true` — completely ignoring the client's actual Accept header.

## Failing test

Added in `test/server/tools.test.ts`:

```
accepts('application/json') returns false when lowercase 'accept' header is 'text/plain'
```

Run `yarn test` and look for that test name in the `tools` describe block.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/server/tools.ts
const acceptHeader = this.headers.Accept; // ← should be this.headers.accept
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `this.headers.Accept` is replaced by a case-insensitive lookup (or lowercased key lookup) so that `accept`, `Accept`, and `ACCEPT` all work
- [ ] The previously failing test passes
- [ ] All other `accepts()` tests continue to pass

title: Bug: Dispatcher proxy() always throws when request body is present
body:
The `proxy()` helper inside `Dispatcher.request()` is meant to reject non-JSON requests with a helpful error. The guard is:

```ts
if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
  throw new Error(...);
}
```

The problem is `headers.contentType` (camelCase). HTTP headers use kebab-case (`content-type`), and the `headers` object never has a `contentType` key. `headers.contentType` is always `undefined`, so `undefined !== "application/json"` is always `true`.

The entire condition reduces to `body !== undefined`, meaning the proxy throws for **every** request that carries a body — including valid `application/json` POST requests.

## Failing test

Added in `test/server/dispatcher.proxy.test.ts`:

```
does not throw when proxying a POST request with a JSON body and content-type: application/json
```

Run `yarn test` and look for that test name in the `a dispatcher passes a proxy function to the operation` describe block.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/server/dispatcher.ts
if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
  //                             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ should be headers["content-type"]
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `headers.contentType` is replaced with `headers["content-type"]`
- [ ] The previously failing test passes
- [ ] The existing proxy test continues to pass
- [ ] A POST request with a non-JSON content type is still rejected with the descriptive error

title: Bug: Tools.accepts() fails when Accept header has spaces after commas
body:
A well-formed HTTP Accept header commonly separates values with `", "` (comma followed by a space), e.g. `"text/html, application/json"`.

`Tools.accepts()` splits on `","` but does **not** trim whitespace from each part. This produces `[" application/json"]` (with a leading space) as the second element. When that is further split on `"/"`, the type becomes `" application"` rather than `"application"`, so the comparison against the requested content type always fails and `accepts()` returns `false` even when the type is listed in the Accept header.

## Failing test

Added in `test/server/tools.test.ts`:

```
accepts('application/json') returns true when Accept header is 'text/html, application/json' (with space)
```

Run `yarn test` and look for that test name in the `tools` describe block.

## Root cause

```ts
// src/server/tools.ts
const acceptTypes = String(acceptHeader).split(",");
return acceptTypes.some((acceptType) => {
  const [type, subtype] = acceptType.split("/"); // " application" has a leading space
  ...
});
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each token is trimmed (e.g. `acceptType.trim()`) before being split on `"/"`
- [ ] The previously failing test passes
- [ ] All other `accepts()` tests continue to pass

title: Fix: Dispatcher proxy() always throws when request body is present
body:
`proxy()` in the Dispatcher was broken in two ways: `headers.contentType` (camelCase) was used instead of `headers["content-type"]` (kebab-case), causing the guard to always evaluate as `true`; and the guard itself unnecessarily restricted proxying to `application/json` requests only.

## Summary

Remove the content-type restriction from `proxy()` entirely so it works for all content types. Rather than re-serializing the parsed body, `proxy()` now forwards `ctx.request.rawBody` — the original wire bytes stored by `koa-bodyparser` before parsing — directly to `fetch()`. This eliminates all re-serialization and correctly handles every content type, including those with charset suffixes (e.g. `application/json; charset=utf-8`).

```ts
// Before (broken — threw for every request with a body)
if (body !== undefined && headers.contentType !== "application/json") {
  throw new Error(`$.proxy() is currently limited to application/json requests...`);
}
body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body),

// After — no restriction, no re-serialization; raw wire bytes forwarded as-is
body: body === undefined ? undefined : rawBody,
```

`koa-bodyparser` unconditionally sets `returnRawBody: true` on `co-body` internally, so `ctx.request.rawBody` is always available as the unparsed string for any request that has a body.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`proxy()` in the Dispatcher had a guard that threw when the request body was present and the content-type was not `application/json`. The guard used `headers.contentType` (camelCase) instead of `headers["content-type"]` (kebab-case), so it was always `undefined`, making the condition always `true` — causing `proxy()` to throw for every request carrying a body, including valid `application/json` POSTs.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/json` and a JSON body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and a JSON body successfully proxies through (charset suffix handled correctly)
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: text/plain` and a plain-text body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `POST /any-route` with `content-type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and a body successfully proxies through without throwing
- [ ] `GET /any-route` with no body proxies normally (unchanged behavior)
- [ ] The upstream response body and headers are returned correctly regardless of content type

## Tasks

- Remove the content-type restriction guard from `proxy()` in `src/server/dispatcher.ts`
- Add `rawBody?: string` to `DispatcherRequest` type
- In `koa-middleware.ts`, declare `rawBody` on the Koa `Request` interface, destructure `ctx.request.rawBody`, and pass it through to `dispatcher.request()` (excluded for GET/HEAD, consistent with `body`)
- In `dispatcher.ts`, destructure `rawBody` in `request()` and use `body === undefined ? undefined : rawBody` in `proxy()` — no re-serialization of any kind
- Update tests: pass `rawBody` alongside `body` and verify the exact string forwarded to upstream `fetch` is the raw wire bytes unchanged

title: fix: Tools.accepts() case-insensitive accept header lookup
body:
`Tools.accepts()` read `this.headers.Accept` (capital A), but Node.js normalizes all incoming HTTP header names to lowercase. In production, `this.headers.Accept` is always `undefined`, triggering the early-return guard and making `accepts()` unconditionally return `true`.

## Summary

Replace the direct key lookup with a case-insensitive search so `accept`, `Accept`, and `ACCEPT` all resolve correctly.

```ts
// Before — broken in production (Node.js lowercases all headers)
const acceptHeader = this.headers.Accept;

// After — handles any casing
const acceptHeader = Object.entries(this.headers).find(
  ([key]) => key.toLowerCase() === "accept",
)?.[1];
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`Tools.accepts()` reads `this.headers.Accept` (capital A). Node.js normalises all incoming HTTP header names to **lowercase**, so when a real HTTP request is processed via Koa the header is stored under `accept` (lowercase). `this.headers.Accept` is therefore always `undefined` in production.

Because `undefined` triggers the early-return guard `if (acceptHeader === "" || acceptHeader === undefined) { return true; }`, the method unconditionally returns `true` — completely ignoring the client's actual Accept header.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `Tools.accepts("application/json")` returns `false` when the request carries a lowercase `accept: text/plain` header
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("text/html")` returns `true` when the request carries `accept: text/html`
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("text/html")` returns `true` when the request carries `Accept: text/html` (capital A, e.g. from a browser or curl)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts("application/json")` returns `true` when no `accept` header is present (existing permissive behavior unchanged)
- [ ] A route handler that gates response type on `tools.accepts()` returns `406 Not Acceptable` when the client sends an incompatible `accept` header in a real Koa request

## Tasks

- Added failing test: `accepts('application/json') returns false when lowercase 'accept' header is 'text/plain'`
- Replaced `this.headers.Accept` with a case-insensitive `Object.entries()` lookup in `src/server/tools.ts`

title: Fix Tools.accepts() failing when Accept header has spaces after commas
body:
`Tools.accepts()` incorrectly returned `false` for valid Accept headers like `"text/html, application/json"` because tokens weren't trimmed after splitting on `","`, leaving a leading space that broke the type comparison.

## Summary

Single-char fix: `.trim()` each token before splitting on `"/"`.

```ts
// Before
const [type, subtype] = acceptType.split("/");
// After
const [type, subtype] = acceptType.trim().split("/");
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`Tools.accepts()` splits on `","` but does not trim whitespace from each part. This produces `[" application/json"]` (with a leading space) as the second element. When that is further split on `"/"`, the type becomes `" application"` rather than `"application"`, so the comparison always fails and `accepts()` returns `false` even when the type is listed in the Accept header.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `Tools.accepts('application/json')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/html, application/json"` (space after comma)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('text/html')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/html"` (no change to single-type behavior)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('text/html')` returns `true` when Accept header is `"text/*"` (wildcard subtype still works)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('application/json')` returns `false` when Accept header is `"text/*"` (rejection still works)
- [ ] `Tools.accepts('what/ever')` returns `true` when Accept header is `undefined` (missing header still accepts all)

## Tasks

- Added `.trim()` to each `acceptType` token before splitting on `"/"` in `src/server/tools.ts`
- Added test case for space-separated Accept header to the `it.each` truth table in `test/server/tools.test.ts`

body:
This PR was opened by the [Changesets release](https://github.com/changesets/action) GitHub action. When you're ready to do a release, you can merge this and the packages will be published to npm automatically. If you're not ready to do a release yet, that's fine, whenever you add more changesets to main, this PR will be updated.


# Releases
## counterfact@2.7.0

### Minor Changes

-   0043b20: Add support for a `counterfact.yaml` config file. All CLI options can now be specified in a `counterfact.yaml` file in the current working directory. Command-line options always take precedence over config file settings. Use `--config <path>` to load a config file from a non-default location.

-   2cbd0d5: Add .empty() method to response builder for responses with no body

-   965dc4e: Add `.apply` REPL dot-command (Approach 1: Minimalist Function Injection).

    The `.apply` command lets you run scenario scripts from the REPL prompt without leaving the terminal. A scenario is a plain TypeScript (or JavaScript) file that exports named functions. Each function receives an `ApplyContext` object with `{ context, loadContext, routes, route }` and can freely read or mutate state.

    **Path resolution:**

    | Command              | File                   | Function |
    | -------------------- | ---------------------- | -------- |
    | `.apply foo`         | `scenarios/index.ts`   | `foo`    |
    | `.apply foo/bar`     | `scenarios/foo.ts`     | `bar`    |
    | `.apply foo/bar/baz` | `scenarios/foo/bar.ts` | `baz`    |

    The `ApplyContext` type is written to `types/apply-context.ts` during code generation.

-   a356bdf: Validate response headers at runtime and report type errors as `response-type-error` HTTP headers (one per error, multiple headers with the same name). Use --no-validate-response to disable.

### Patch Changes

-   54b866c: add docs/usage-patterns.md documenting seven usage patterns: explore a new API, simulate failures and edge cases, mock APIs with dummy data, fast sandbox for agentic coding, hybrid proxy, API reference implementation, and executable spec
-   6e0655b: fix type error when returning a response with no body (e.g. `$.response[200]` or `$.response[404]` in routes where the spec defines no response body)
-   754dbbd: add two new usage pattern docs: Automated Integration Tests (programmatic API in test suites) and Custom Middleware (\_.middleware.ts for cross-cutting concerns); propose three future patterns as GitHub issues: Record and Replay, Webhook Simulation, and Persistent State
-   f9a9790: Refactor `src/counterfact-types/` so that each type lives in its own file with a JSDoc comment explaining its purpose. The `index.ts` now re-exports all types from the individual files. This is an internal refactor with no change to the public API.
-   6d50ae6: Updated dependency `ajv` to `8.18.0`.
-   fa25ec3: Updated dependency `@swc/core` to `1.15.24`.
-   cbab929: Updated dependency `eslint` to `10.2.0`.
-   9c5fc1d: Replace deprecated `unescape()` with `decodeURIComponent()` wrapped in a try/catch in `requirement.ts`. This avoids use of the deprecated global function while preserving the behavior of returning invalid percent-encoded sequences unchanged.
-   323cf1c: Revised documentation for coherence: added table of contents to usage, reference, and FAQ pages; added "See also" sections to pages that were missing them; moved the usage guide link from the README footer into the "Go deeper" table.

title: Add CI workflow to automatically update pull request branches when `main` changes
body:
## Context
Pull requests can fall behind `main`, which creates drift and delays feedback until late in the process.  

GitHub provides a manual “Update branch” button, but it relies on humans remembering to click it.  

We want a deterministic, CI-driven approach that keeps PR branches up to date automatically whenever `main` is updated.  

This aligns with our goal of reducing variation and enforcing correctness through automation rather than habit.  

## Goal
Automatically update all open pull request branches when `main` receives new commits.  

## Requirements
• Trigger on push to `main`  
• Find all open pull requests  
• Attempt to update each PR branch using GitHub’s native update mechanism  
• Do not fail the workflow if a PR cannot be updated (e.g., conflicts)  
• Log which PRs were updated vs skipped  
• Respect branch protection rules  
• No local git merge/rebase logic (use GitHub API only)  
• Skip PRs created by Renovate  

## Implementation Approach
Create a GitHub Actions workflow that:  

1. Runs on `push` to `main`  
2. Uses `actions/github-script` to:  
   • List open PRs  
   • Skip PRs where `pr.user.login === "renovate[bot]"`  
   • Call `pulls.updateBranch` for the rest  

## Proposed Workflow
```yaml
name: Update PR branches

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  update-prs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - name: Update PR branches
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const { data: pulls } = await github.rest.pulls.list({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              state: "open"
            });

            for (const pr of pulls) {
              // Skip Renovate PRs
              if (pr.user?.login === "renovate[bot]") {
                console.log(`Skipped PR #${pr.number} (Renovate)`);
                continue;
              }

              try {
                await github.rest.pulls.updateBranch({
                  owner: context.repo.owner,
                  repo: context.repo.repo,
                  pull_number: pr.number
                });
                console.log(`Updated PR #${pr.number}`);
              } catch (e) {
                console.log(`Skipped PR #${pr.number}: ${e.message}`);
              }
            }
```

## Acceptance Criteria
• When a commit is pushed to `main`, the workflow runs automatically  
• Open PRs that are behind `main` are updated  
• PRs created by Renovate are skipped  
• PRs with conflicts are skipped without failing the workflow  
• Workflow logs clearly show which PRs were updated or skipped  
• No unexpected force pushes or rebases occur  
• Workflow completes successfully even if some PRs cannot be updated  

## Notes
• This uses GitHub’s native “Update branch” behavior (merge, not rebase)  
• Conflicts are expected and should be handled manually  
• Future enhancement: allow opt-in via label (e.g., `auto-update`) to limit scope  

## Manual Acceptance Tests
- [ ] Create a PR and merge a change into `main` → PR branch updates automatically  
- [ ] Create a PR opened by Renovate → workflow skips it  
- [ ] Create a PR with a merge conflict → workflow skips it and logs the reason  
- [ ] Verify no workflow failures when some PRs cannot be updated  
- [ ] Confirm branch protection rules are respected

title: Replace PR auto-update workflow with merge queue
body:
## Context
We currently use a CI workflow that automatically updates all open pull request branches when `main` changes.  

This was intended to keep PRs up to date and ensure required checks run against the latest base branch.  

In practice, this approach introduces complexity and inconsistency:  

• Required checks do not always trigger when branches are updated via automation (due to `GITHUB_TOKEN` behavior)  
• Developers sometimes need to close/reopen PRs to retrigger checks  
• The system relies on updating every PR rather than validating at merge time  

GitHub merge queue provides a built-in, deterministic alternative that validates changes against the latest `main` at merge time without requiring branch updates.  

## Goal
Remove the PR auto-update workflow and replace it with GitHub merge queue as the primary mechanism for ensuring PRs are up to date and validated.  

## Scope

### Remove
• Delete the existing workflow that updates PR branches on `main` push  
• Remove any related documentation or references  

### Add / Update

#### 1. Enable merge queue
• Enable “Require a merge queue” in branch protection rules for `main`  
• Ensure required status checks are still configured  

#### 2. Update all required workflows
Modify all workflows that produce required checks to support merge queue by adding the `merge_group` trigger.  

Example:

```yaml
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
```

#### 3. Validate required check names
• Ensure required checks in branch protection match actual job names  
• Confirm checks are emitted for both `pull_request` and `merge_group` events  

#### 4. Review workflow filters
• Remove or adjust `paths`, `branches`, or other filters that could prevent workflows from running for merge queue commits  
• Ensure workflows reliably run for merge group events  

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Bug Hunt 2: Document three latent bugs as issue proposals
body:
Searched the codebase for latent bugs and created three issue proposals under `.github/issue-proposals/` for automated conversion to GitHub issues on merge.

## Bugs found

- **`parseInt` receives an array** (`bin/counterfact.js:44`): `process.versions.node.split(".")` returns an array passed directly to `Number.parseInt()`. Works by accident via implicit `.toString()` coercion (`"22,3,0"` → parses `22`). Should be `.split(".")[0]`.

- **XML text content not escaped** (`src/server/json-to-xml.ts:89`): Primitive values are embedded verbatim as XML text content — `xmlEscape()` is defined and used for attributes in the same file but omitted for element text. Strings with `<`, `>`, `&`, etc. produce malformed XML.

- **Deprecated `unescape()` used** (`src/typescript-generator/requirement.ts:64`): `unescape` (deprecated since ES3) decodes percent-encoded JSON Pointer segments. Should be replaced with `decodeURIComponent` wrapped in try/catch (handles non-standard `%uXXXX` without throwing).

title: Bug: XML text content is not escaped in json-to-xml.ts
body:
In `src/server/json-to-xml.ts`, the `jsonToXml` function correctly escapes attribute values using `xmlEscape()`, but omits escaping for plain text content (the fallback branch that handles primitive values such as strings, numbers, and booleans):

```ts
// src/server/json-to-xml.ts  line 89
return `<${name}>${String(json)}</${name}>`;
```

If `json` is a string that contains XML special characters — `<`, `>`, `&`, `'`, or `"` — the output will be malformed XML. For example:

```ts
jsonToXml('<script>alert("xss")</script>', undefined, "item")
// → <item><script>alert("xss")</script></item>   ← invalid XML
```

The file already defines `xmlEscape()` and uses it for attribute values (line 57). The fix is to apply the same function to text content:

```ts
return `<${name}>${xmlEscape(String(json))}</${name}>`;
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `xmlEscape()` is applied to primitive text values in the final return of `jsonToXml`
- [ ] A unit test confirms that strings containing `<`, `>`, `&`, `'`, and `"` are correctly escaped in element text content
- [ ] Attribute values (already escaped) continue to pass their existing tests
- [ ] Existing XML generation tests continue to pass

title: Fix CI script that creates issues
body:
## Summary

Three bugs in the issue-creation workflow: test fixture files were being processed as real proposals; sub-issue linking was silently failing because the GitHub sub-issues API requires the internal issue `id`, not the human-readable `number`; and processed proposal files were not being deleted from the repository because the `git push` back to `main` was failing (the checkout lacked the credentials required to push through branch protection).

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

There are two problems:

1. It is creating two extraneous example issues.
2. It is not attaching issues to the parent issue (parentIssueId in the frontmatter)

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] A new issue proposal merged to `main` is created as a GitHub issue
- [ ] The created issue appears as a sub-issue of the `parentIssue` specified in the proposal's front matter
- [ ] No extraneous "Example Issue One" or "Example Issue Two" issues are created on merge
- [ ] A proposal without `parentIssue` but with an issue number in the branch name still gets linked to the correct parent
- [ ] A proposal file is deleted from the repo after successful issue creation

## Tasks

- **Deleted** `example-issue-one.md` and `example-issue-two.md` — these test fixtures were live in the proposals directory and being processed on every merge (they persisted because the cleanup commit was not being pushed successfully)
- **Fixed `create_github_issue`** to extract `.id` alongside `.number` from the GitHub API response; the sub-issues REST API (`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{n}/sub_issues`) requires `sub_issue_id` to be the internal integer ID (`.id`), not the issue number (`.number`)
- **Updated `add_sub_issue`** parameter renamed from `child_number` → `child_issue_id` to make the distinction explicit
- **Fixed `create-issues.yml`** to check out with `token: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (matching the pattern in `renovate-changesets.yaml`) so the bot has permission to push the file-deletion commit back to `main`; also added `git pull --rebase` before `git push` to handle race conditions

```python
# Before — wrong: passes issue number (e.g. 42) as sub_issue_id
issue_number, issue_url = create_github_issue(...)
add_sub_issue(repo, parent_issue, issue_number)

# After — correct: passes internal ID (e.g. 2168781765) as sub_issue_id
issue_number, issue_id, issue_url = create_github_issue(...)
add_sub_issue(repo, parent_issue, issue_id)
```

title: Bug: Deprecated unescape() function used in requirement.ts
Bug: parseInt() receives an array instead of a string in Node version check
body:
In `bin/counterfact.js`, the Node.js version check passes the result of `String.prototype.split()` — an array — directly to `Number.parseInt()`:

```js
// bin/counterfact.js
if (Number.parseInt(process.versions.node.split("."), 10) < MIN_NODE_VERSION) {
```

`process.versions.node.split(".")` returns an array like `["22", "3", "0"]`. When this is passed to `Number.parseInt()`, JavaScript implicitly calls `.toString()` on it, producing the string `"22,3,0"`. `parseInt` then parses up to the first non-numeric character (the comma), yielding `22`. This happens to give the correct major version **by accident**.

The correct code is:

```js
if (Number.parseInt(process.versions.node.split(".")[0], 10) < MIN_NODE_VERSION) {
```

While the current code produces the right result today, it:
- Relies on implicit coercion that is hard to reason about
- Would silently produce wrong results if the version string format changes
- Is a clear programming error that could confuse contributors

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `process.versions.node.split(".")[0]` (array index `[0]`) is used instead of passing the whole array to `parseInt`
- [ ] The version guard still exits with an error message when run on a Node version below the minimum
- [ ] Existing tests continue to pass

title: fix: replace deprecated unescape() with decodeURIComponent() in requirement.ts
fix: use `split(".")[0]` instead of passing whole array to `parseInt` in Node version check
body:
## Summary

`process.versions.node.split(".")` returns an array; passing it directly to `Number.parseInt()` relies on implicit `.toString()` coercion (`["22","3","0"]` → `"22,3,0"`) which happens to parse correctly today but is fragile and misleading.

**Fix:** add `[0]` to extract only the major version string before parsing, and reformat the `if` condition to satisfy Prettier's line-length rules.

```js
// before
Number.parseInt(process.versions.node.split("."), 10)

// after
if (
  Number.parseInt(process.versions.node.split(".")[0], 10) < MIN_NODE_VERSION
) {
```

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

`process.versions.node.split(".")` returns an array; passing it directly to `Number.parseInt()` relies on implicit `.toString()` coercion (`["22","3","0"]` → `"22,3,0"`) which happens to parse correctly today but is fragile and misleading. Fix by adding `[0]` to extract only the major version string before parsing.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] Running `counterfact` on a supported Node version starts the server normally without any version-related error
- [ ] Simulating a Node version below 17 (e.g. by temporarily lowering `MIN_NODE_VERSION`) prints the expected error message and exits

- Reformatted the `if` condition in `bin/counterfact.js` to a multi-line form to satisfy Prettier's line-length requirement

title: ADR for the .apply REPL command
body:
## Summary

An Architecture Decision Record (ADR) is added at `docs/adr/001-apply-command-with-function-injection.md` documenting the selection of Solution 1 (Minimalist Function Injection) for the `.apply` REPL command. The two temporary proposal files for approaches 2 and 3 are removed; the ADR is the permanent record.

The remaining proposal file (`apply-approach-1-function-injection.md`) has been refined based on review feedback:

- Base directory corrected from `repl/` to `scenarios/`
- `ApplyContext` is a generated type that lives in `./types/`; always the same shape in v1, will incorporate `_.context.ts` types in future iterations
- Feedback output simplified to just `Applied <path>` — no route diff for the first iteration
- All snapshot/diff references removed from the implementation sketch and acceptance criteria

The ADR Advice section attributes all AI-authored bullets with `(Copilot/Claude)` and includes a new `(@pmcelhaney)` bullet noting that the function return value (currently `void`) is a natural extension point — it could return an optional summary string or an object with a `teardown()` function.

The path/name convention is documented consistently across all remaining files:

```
.apply foo          # scenarios/index.ts  → foo($)
.apply foo/bar      # scenarios/foo.ts    → bar($)
.apply foo/bar/baz  # scenarios/foo/bar.ts → baz($)
```

<details>

title: Multiple APIs
body:
A server may need to support multiple APIs, defined by multiple OpenAPI specs. We need to define a clean way to pass multiple API documents. Each API will be served under a different path. Make sure there are no clashes in the generated types. 

Think about the implications of multiple APIs. 

1. How will the root path of each API be determined? We want the user to be able to specify the root path for each API. If they don't specify the root path choose a reasonable default. We want to support OpenAPI 2.x and 3.x.

2. How will the layout of the generated code be affected? 

3. Anything else I'm not thinking about. 

Create three designs to solve multiple APIs. Document each one in a new issue.

title: Add draft ADR for multiple API support (#1718)
body:
## Summary

Issue #1718 asks for three distinct designs for running multiple OpenAPI specs under a single Counterfact server. This PR documents those designs as a draft Architecture Decision Record (ADR) under `docs/adr/`. No decision has been taken yet; the ADR captures all three options for review and discussion.

<details>

A server may need to support multiple APIs, defined by multiple OpenAPI specs. We need to define a clean way to pass multiple API documents. Each API will be served under a different path. Make sure there are no clashes in the generated types.

1. How will the root path of each API be determined? We want the user to be able to specify the root path for each API. If they don't specify the root path choose a reasonable default. We want to support OpenAPI 2.x and 3.x.
2. How will the layout of the generated code be affected?
3. Anything else I'm not thinking about.

Create three designs to solve multiple APIs. Document each one in a new issue.

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [ ] `docs/adr/xxx-multiple-api-support.md` exists with Status: Draft and a non-empty body
- [ ] All three options address root-path determination (explicit prefix → `basePath`/`servers[]` → fallback)
- [ ] All three options describe a generated code layout that prevents type-name collisions and supports a shared root `_.context.ts`
- [ ] Each option is meaningfully distinct (CLI `prefix+spec` flag vs. typed config file vs. workspace directory convention)
- [ ] Backwards compatibility with today's single-spec usage is addressed in every option
- [ ] Cross-cutting concerns (REPL, Swagger UI, watch mode, Dispatcher) are covered in the ADR

title: Propose improvements to make Counterfact more useful for AI agents
body:
Counterfact is increasingly being used in workflows where AI agents (e.g., Copilot, LLM-based agents) are building, testing, and iterating on applications that depend on APIs.

We want to make Counterfact a first-class environment for agents — fast, predictable, and easy to reason about.

Your task is to analyze the current design of Counterfact and propose improvements that would make it more effective for AI agents.

⸻

Objective

Generate a set of actionable GitHub issues that describe improvements to Counterfact for agent-driven development workflows.

Each suggestion should be written as a standalone GitHub issue that could be implemented independently.

⸻

Context

AI agents interacting with APIs have different needs than human developers:
	•	They rely heavily on contracts (OpenAPI)
	•	They benefit from deterministic and inspectable behavior
	•	They struggle with hidden state and implicit side effects
	•	They need fast feedback loops and zero-friction environments
	•	They perform best when systems are self-describing and discoverable

Counterfact already provides:
	•	OpenAPI-driven type safety
	•	Local, fast simulation
	•	Stateful context
	•	REPL for runtime interaction

We want to extend this so that agents can:
	•	Understand how to use the API without guessing
	•	Safely explore behavior
	•	Recover from mistakes
	•	Generate correct code with minimal iteration

⸻

Instructions
	1.	Analyze Counterfact from the perspective of an AI agent building an app against an API.
	2.	Identify gaps, friction points, or missing capabilities.
	3.	Propose improvements.

⸻

Output Format

Create multiple Markdown files, one per proposed improvement.

Each file should:
	•	Live in a new folder: .github/proposed-issues/
	•	Use front matter for metadata
	•	Follow this structure:

---
title: "<clear, actionable title>"
labels: ["enhancement", "agent-experience"]
parent issue: <this issue number>
---

## Summary
Brief description of the improvement.

## Problem
What problem does this solve for AI agents?

## Proposed Solution
What should be built or changed?

## Example
Concrete example (code, CLI, or workflow).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clear, testable outcomes
- [ ] Behavior is deterministic where possible
- [ ] Improves agent success rate or reduces iteration


⸻

Areas to Explore (not exhaustive)

Focus on high-leverage improvements such as:
	•	Discoverability (e.g., how an agent learns what’s possible)
	•	Determinism vs randomness
	•	State inspection and control
	•	Error simulation and recovery
	•	REPL ergonomics for agents
	•	Contract clarity and enforcement
	•	Testability and automation hooks
	•	Agent-friendly documentation or metadata
	•	CLI / programmatic interfaces
	•	Debuggability and traceability

⸻

Constraints
	•	Do not modify existing code
	•	Only generate proposed issues
	•	Keep each issue focused and independently implementable
	•	Prefer practical, high-impact improvements over theoretical ideas

⸻

Goal

Produce a set of well-structured issues that, if implemented, would make Counterfact the best possible environment for AI agents building against APIs.

⸻

title: Add a config file
body:
The options in the command line are getting unwieldy. It's time to support a counterfact.yaml file as an alternative way to set configuration. 

Follow common conventions, e.g. --config to set an alternate config file path; when there's a conflict, command line settings override config file settings

title: feat: add counterfact.yaml config file support with --config option
body:
## Summary

CLI options were becoming unwieldy to pass on every invocation. This adds a `counterfact.yaml` config file as an alternative — any CLI option can now be set there, with command-line flags always winning on conflict.

```yaml
# counterfact.yaml
spec: ./openapi.yaml
port: 8080
serve: true
watch: true
proxy-url: https://api.example.com
prefix: /api/v1
```

Use `--config <path>` to point at a non-default location.

<details>
<summary>Original Prompt</summary>

The options in the command line are getting unwieldy. It's time to support a counterfact.yaml file as an alternative way to set configuration.

Follow common conventions, e.g. --config to set an alternate config file path; when there's a conflict, command line settings override config file settings

</details>

## Manual acceptance tests

- [x] Running with a `counterfact.yaml` in the current directory starts the server using config values (e.g. `port: 8080` overrides the default 3100)
- [x] An explicit CLI flag (e.g. `--port 9000`) overrides the same key set in `counterfact.yaml`
- [x] `--config ./path/to/other.yaml` loads options from the specified file instead of `counterfact.yaml`
- [x] `--config ./nonexistent.yaml` exits with a clear "Config file not found" error
- [x] No `counterfact.yaml` present and no `--config` flag → startup proceeds normally with CLI/default values
- [x] Kebab-case keys in the YAML (e.g. `proxy-url`, `always-fake-optionals`) are recognised correctly

## Tasks

- Added `src/util/load-config-file.ts`: reads and parses YAML, normalises kebab-case keys to camelCase, returns `{}` when default file is absent, throws when a required file is missing
- Updated `bin/counterfact.js`: imports `loadConfigFile`, adds `--config <path>` Commander option, merges file config into options before building `Config` using `program.getOptionValueSource()` to detect explicit CLI flags
- Added 9 unit tests in `test/util/load-config-file.test.ts` using `usingTemporaryFiles()` per project convention
- Updated `README.md` and `bin/README.md` with the new option and example config
- Updated `docs/usage.md`: added `--config` to the CLI reference block and a new "Using a counterfact.yaml config file" `<details>` section covering the example YAML, kebab-case key normalisation, custom config path, and missing-file behaviour
- Added minor changeset

title: Tag design PRs
body:
When an agent works on the issue and the goal of the issue is to create more issues rather than write code, the agent should tag the PR and the issue with the label "design". 

Also in such cases Copilot should not add manual acceptance criteria. 

Update the copilot instructions to reflect that. 

Also when a PR is tagged "design" the CI script checking manual acceptance criteria should pass when no manual acceptance credentials are found.
